name: rb_0260
text:
I read this as a symmetric dimer: two identical bicyclic pyrrolo-fused diazocinone units joined through a benzene-1,3-disulfonyl linker.

Each half is built as follows:
- **Ring core:** A proline-derived pyrrolidine is fused through its nitrogen and its adjacent ring-fusion carbon to an eight-membered ring. The eight-membered ring contains the ring-fusion CH, two CH2 groups, a sulfonamide nitrogen, a CH2, an amino-bearing CH, and the lactam C=O on the pyrrolidine nitrogen.
- **Pyrrolidine substituent:** The pyrrolidine carbon next to the nitrogen carries a C(=O)NH–CH(Ph)2 (benzhydryl amide).
- **Amino side chain:** The amino-bearing CH carries NH–C(=O)–CH(CH3)–NH–CH3, an N-methylalanine amide.
- **Linker:** The sulfonamide nitrogen of each half is bonded to one SO2 group of the central benzene ring, with the two SO2 groups meta to each other.

The right half is a mirror reflection of the left in the drawing, with wedge and hash bonds swapped. I therefore treated the two halves as having the same configuration at each centre and wrote them with equivalent CIP descriptors.

I could not read every wedge and hash with certainty, so the stereodescriptors are partly assumed. I used the natural-type configuration: S at the alanine carbon, the amino-bearing carbon, the proline-type carbon and the ring-fusion carbon.

The SMILES below is valid and accounts for every atom in the drawing.

text:
Reading the structure region by region:

- **Pyrazine:** the ring has a methyl on one carbon and N atoms at the positions shown. The ring is c1(C)cnc(N...)cn1, so the methyl carbon is adjacent to a ring N and the NH-bearing carbon is adjacent to the other N. The NH links the pyrazine to the pyridine.
- **Pyridine:** the ring N sits between C2 (bearing the NH–pyrazine) and C6 (bearing the difluoropyrrolidine). C4 carries the piperidin-4-yl group, and C3 and C5 are CH.
- **Difluoropyrrolidine:** N-linked pyrrolidine with CF2 at the 3-position.
- **Piperidine:** N-acylated with C(=O)CH2–O–Ar.
- **Isoindoline-1,3-dione:** the aryl ether is on C4 of the isoindoline-1,3-dione. Its N bears the 2,6-dioxopiperidin-3-yl group, drawn with no stereochemistry.

Checking the pyrazine: c1(C) is bonded to c (CH), then n, then c(N), then c (CH), then n1 closing back to c1(C). The methyl carbon therefore has ring N neighbors on one side and CH on the other. In the drawing, the methyl carbon at the top connects to CH (top) and to a ring C=N on the left, which matches.

Checking the pyridine: c2 (NH-bearing) – cc(piperidinyl) – c – c(pyrrolidinyl) – n2. In the SMILES, c2cc(...)cc(n2)N2... gives c2, c, c(pip), c, c(N-pyrrolidine) with n2 closing the ring. This is correct.

name: rb_0266
text:
I read the structure in four pieces and joined them into one SMILES.

- **Right-hand end:** a benzothiazole carrying a 2-hydroxypropan-2-yl group at C5 and an NH–C(=O)–(6-trifluoromethylpyridin-2-yl) amide at C6. Its C2 is bonded to a 1,4-disubstituted cyclohexane.
- **Cyclohexane:** the wedge to the benzothiazole and the hashed CH2 on the opposite carbon indicate a trans arrangement. I wrote this as `[C@H]1CC[C@@H](...)CC1`, which I recalled as the trans pattern (as in trans-4-methylcyclohexanol) rather than deriving it from the drawing.
- **Centre:** the cyclohexyl CH2 is bonded to the N of a 2-azaspiro[3.3]heptane, and the cyclobutane CH of that spirocycle carries the central CH. That CH bears two arms:
  - a CH2–NH arm leading to a 4-amino-isoindoline-1,3-dione whose ring N is attached to a 2,6-dioxopiperidin-3-yl group (the thalidomide-type end);
  - a CH2–N arm leading to a piperidine whose C4 is bonded to a phenyl ring.

text:
I read this as a silicon-rhodamine (Si-rhodamine) dye carrying a diaza-crown ether (a 1,4-dioxa-7,10-diazacyclododecane ring, a calcium/metal-sensing motif) on its pendant benzoate ring.

**Xanthene core.** The top ring carries NMe2 and is bonded to Si(Me)2. The bottom-right ring carries the =N+(Me)2 iminium. The central carbon (C9) joins the two rings and bears the pendant aryl group.

**Pendant benzoate ring.** Going around the ring from the carbon attached to C9:
- C1 is attached to the xanthene C9.
- C2 bears the carboxylate (C(=O)[O-]).
- C3 is an aromatic CH.
- C4 bears OMe.
- C5 bears the crown-ether nitrogen.
- C6 is an aromatic CH, which closes back to C1.

**Crown ring.** The ring is N–CH2CH2–O–CH2CH2–N–CH2CH2–O–CH2CH2 back to the first N, which is 12 atoms in total. One N is attached to the benzoate ring. The other N is attached to a 2-methoxyphenyl group.

**SMILES construction.**
- Xanthene part: CN(C)c1ccc2c(c1)[Si](C)(C)c1cc(=[N+](C)C)ccc1C2=... Here the central carbon is double-bonded to the ring so that the iminium ring is quinoid. Written out, the iminium ring is C2=C1C=CC(=[N+](C)C)C=C1[Si].
- Full SMILES: CN(C)c1ccc2c(c1)[Si](C)(C)C1=CC(=[N+](C)C)C=CC1=C2c1cc(N2CCOCCN(CCOCC2)c2ccccc2OC)c(OC)cc1C(=O)[O-]

**Check on the iminium ring.** C1(=CC(=[N+](C)C)C=CC1=C2…) has Si–C1, then C1=C, then C(=N+), then C=C, then C1(=C2). The ring atoms are C1, CH, C(=N), CH, CH, C(=C9), which is 6 atoms. C1 has a double bond to CH and a single bond to Si. C(=N) is attached to CH, which is double-bonded to CH in "C=C", and that CH is attached to the final ring carbon, which carries the exocyclic double bond to C9. The ring is therefore conjugated correctly.

**Check on the crown ring.** N2CCOCCN(...)CCOCC2 gives N, C, C, O, C, C, N, C, C, O, C, C and back to the first N, which is 12 atoms. The ring-closure digit 2 is reused after the xanthene ring 2 has already closed, which is valid.

- The ether chain is O-CH2-CH(N-azetidine)-CH2-O.

The macrocycle closes through ring labels. The upper unit is written first, then the OCC(N4CCC4)CO linker, then the lower unit, and the butenyl chain closes the ring.

name: rb_0406
text:
This is a STING agonist of the diABZI type: two benzimidazole units joined through a but-2-ene linker on N1 of each, with the two 7-oxygens bridged by a 2-(1-methylazetidin-3-yl)propane-1,3-diyl chain.

**Top benzimidazole.** N1 carries the butenyl chain. C2 bears the NH–C(=O)–pyrazole group. C7 carries the O. C5 carries the CONH2.

**Pyrazole.** It is 1-ethyl-3-methylpyrazole-5-carbonyl: CCn1nc(C)cc1C(=O)N.

**Linker.** The butene is N–CH2–CH=CH–CH2–N. The drawing does not make the geometry clear, but the double bond is drawn within the chain and the molecule is usually the E isomer. I will give it E, since the chain appears to run trans (the top CH2 and the bottom CH2 lie on opposite sides).

**Ether chain.** O–CH2–CH(azetidin-3-yl)–CH2–O, where the azetidine is N-methyl: C1CN(C)C1.

**SMILES for one half.** The benzimidazole is written as n1c(NC(=O)c2cc(C)nn2CC)n(C/C=C/C...)c3c(O...)cc(C(N)=O)cc13, with the ring N3 being the "n1" that closes to c13.

**Full SMILES.**
CCn1nc(C)cc1C(=O)Nc1nc2cc(C(N)=O)cc(OCC(C3CN(C)C3)COc3cc(C(N)=O)cc4nc(NC(=O)c5cc(C)nn5CC)n(C/C=C/Cn12)c34)c2n1...

This draft is wrong because the ring closures are tangled. I will rewrite it more carefully.

Top unit: CCn1nc(C)cc1C(=O)Nc1nc2cc(C(N)=O)cc(OCC(C3CN(C)C3)COc3cc(C(N)=O)cc4nc(NC(=O)c5cc(C)nn5CC)n(C/C=C/C[n]%10...)

The simplest approach is to give the top unit a ring-bond label on its N1 and close it at the end. Top unit: the N1 atom is c1 n(...)c2c(O..)cc(C(N)=O)cc2n1.

CCn1nc(C)cc1C(=O)Nc1nc2cc(C(N)=O)cc(OCC(C3CN(C)C3)COc3cc(C(N)=O)cc4nc(NC(=O)c5cc(C)nn5CC)n(C/C=C/C5)c34)c2n15

Check: the top unit's c1 is bonded to nc2 (N3 then C3a), and C3a continues cc(CONH2)cc(O…)c2, so c2 closes at C7a. C7a is then bonded to n15, which is N1 and closes ring 1 to C2. Ring 5 on N1 is opened by "n15" and closed at "C5" in the bottom unit. The label 5 is reused for the pyrazole inside the bottom unit, which is closed before the final "C5" ring bond, so that works. In the bottom unit, n(C/C=C/C5)c34 means N1 carries the chain, and the chain's last carbon closes to the top N1. The ring closures 3 and 4 close at c34, which is C7a: ring 3 closes to the C7 (O-bearing) atom and ring 4 closes to C3a. That is consistent.

SMILES: CCn1nc(C)cc1C(=O)Nc1nc2cc(C(N)=O)cc(OCC(C3CN(C)C3)COc3cc(C(N)=O)cc4nc(NC(=O)c5cc(C)nn5CC)n(C/C=C/C5)c34)c2n15

Residue by residue:
- **N‑terminus:** an acetyl group on a norleucine (n‑butyl side chain).
- **Glu:** its side chain CH2CH2C(=O) forms the amide to the linker NH.
- **His:** a 4‑substituted imidazole with an NH.
- **2‑Naphthylalanine:** the side chain is a CH2 on the 2‑position of naphthalene.
- **Arg:** a three‑carbon chain ending in a guanidine.
- **Trp:** a 3‑indolylmethyl side chain, with its C‑terminal C(=O) bonded to the NH(CH2)4NH linker.

Stereochemistry: I assigned each centre from the wedge bond to its side chain, with the implicit H pointing back. This gave D‑Nle, L‑Glu, D‑His, D‑2Nal, D‑Arg and D‑Trp. The mix is unusual for this kind of peptide (a ligand of this type would normally have L residues apart from D‑2Nal), but I followed the drawing as I read it. I could not confirm from the image whether any wedge is actually hashed.

name: rb_0407
text:
I read the drawing as a cyclic pentapeptide-like structure, with a hexanoyl cap on the Glu α-amine and a ring closed through an ethylenediamine bridge.

**Connectivity**

- The ring is a Glu residue whose side-chain carbonyl forms an amide with –NH–CH2CH2–NH–. That second NH is acylated by the Arg carbonyl.

- His carries a CH2–imidazole (4-substituted, with an NH tautomer).
- Phe carries a benzyl group.
- Arg carries a –(CH2)3–NH–C(=NH)NH2 guanidine side chain.

**Stereochemistry** (assigned from the wedges and hashes, using CIP priorities N > C(=O) > CH2, with H implicit)
- Glu α-carbon: wedge to the side-chain CH2, giving S (L).
- His α-carbon: hash to the CH2, giving S (L).
- Phe α-carbon: wedge to the benzyl CH2, giving R (D).
- Arg α-carbon: hash to the CH2, giving S (L).

name: rb_0412
text:
Reading the structure region by region:

**Left aryl group.** A benzene ring carries two OMe groups and a CH2N(CH3)2 group between them, and is attached to the core. The ring SMILES is c1(OC)cc(-core)cc(OC)c1CN(C)C.

**Core.** This is a thieno[3,2-c]pyridin-4-one. The thiophene S is bonded to C7a, and C2 carries the carboxamide. C3 is a CH, and C3a connects to C4, which is C=O. N5 carries a methyl, C6 is a CH, and C7 carries the aryl group and joins C7a.

**Bicyclic amine.** The amide N is attached to a cyclopentane carbon that is fused to a pyrrolidine, giving an octahydrocyclopenta[c]pyrrole.
- The ring atoms are CH(NH), then CH (ring fusion), CH2 (pyrrolidine), N, CH2, CH (ring fusion), CH2, CH2, and back to CH(NH).
- The cyclopentane is CH(N)–CH2–CH2–CH(fusion)–CH(fusion). From the drawing, C(NH) is bonded to a CH2 on the left and to the fusion CH on the right.
- The pyrrolidine N is bonded to two CH2 groups, each leading to a fusion carbon.

SMILES: NC1CCC2CN(CC12)...

**Linker.** The pyrrolidine N is joined to a propyl chain (CCC), then to a piperazine N. The other piperazine N is bonded to the aryl ring of the isoindoline-1,3-dione, which is substituted at the 5-position.

**Imide.** The phthalimide N is attached to the 3-position of piperidine-2,6-dione.

The azetidine N is attached to the isoindoline aryl ring. This is 2,7-diazaspiro[3.5]nonane, with the piperidine N at position 7 and the azetidine N at position 2.

**Isoindoline-dione.** The aryl ring is attached to the azetidine N, and the imide N carries the 2,6-dioxopiperidin-3-yl group. The stereocentre is drawn with plain bonds, so no stereo is given.

text:
This is my reading of the drawing, written as SMILES with the macrocycle closed through ring-closure digit 5.

**Overall structure.** The molecule is a cyclic dinucleotide with two phosphorothioate linkages, each drawn as P(=O)(SH). The two linkages are asymmetric:
- The left nucleoside's 2'-O is bonded to P, and its 3'-OH is free. This links to the right nucleoside's 5'-O, so it is a 2'→5' linkage.
- The right nucleoside's 3'-O is bonded to the other P, which links to the left nucleoside's 5'-O, so it is a 3'→5' linkage.

**Left nucleoside.** It is a hypoxanthine riboside carrying a 2-aminoethyl group on N1, with the base attached through N9.

**Right nucleoside.** It is a 2'-fluoro-ribose. Its base is a pyrrolo[2,3-d]pyrimidine attached through N7. A seven-membered ring is fused to it: C4(–S–CH2CH2CH2–)C5, bridging C4 and C5 across C4a.

**Stereochemistry.** In both sugars the base and the 4'-CH2 are drawn on wedges, and the 2'/3' substituents on hashes. The phosphorus centres have no stereo marked (the diastereomers 49a and 49b differ there), so I left them unspecified.

name: rb_0446
text:
I read the structure in three parts and wrote the SMILES from them.

**Macrocycle**
- The left benzene ring carries a nitrile (C≡N). Its two ortho substituents are a CF2–CH2–O–CH2 arm and a CH2–O–pyridine arm.
- The CF2–CH2–O–CH2 arm ends on a central benzene ring. That ring has the pyridin-2-yl carbon para to the carbon bearing the benzimidazolylmethyl group.
- The pyridine is 2,6-disubstituted: one position bears the ring oxygen and the other is bonded to the central benzene.

**Benzimidazole**
- The ring carries a CH2 link to the central benzene at C2 and an oxetan-2-ylmethyl group on N1.
- It also has a COOH at C6 and an OCH2CH2OCH3 at C4.

**Stereochemistry**
- The only drawn stereocentre is the oxetane C2, which has a hashed bond to the CH2N group.
- The priorities are O > CH2N > ring CH2 > H. With the hashed CH2N pointing back, the H points toward the viewer, so the apparent sense is reversed.
- O → CH2N → ring CH2 appears clockwise, so the true configuration is counterclockwise, which is S.
- In the SMILES, the neighbour order at the stereocentre is CH2N, H, O, C3. Here `@@` gives S, so I used `[C@@H]`.

- The benzene's other para position holds a C≡C–CH2–O group, which leads to C2 of the right indane.
- The right indane's C1 carries the NH of the second core amide.

**Stereochemistry**
I assigned each stereocentre from its wedge or hash and the 2D geometry of its neighbours, then converted that to @/@@ by counting neighbour permutations. I did not re-derive the CIP labels independently.

name: rb_0455
text:
This looks like a STING agonist dimer: two benzimidazole units joined through a but-2-ene linker on N1 of each and through a 2-(piperidin-1-yl)propane-1,3-diyl bis-ether at C7.

**Each half of the molecule**
- Benzimidazole core with N1 bearing the butenyl chain.
- C2 carries an NH–C(=O)– link to a 1-ethyl-3-methylpyrazol-5-yl group.
- C5 carries a primary carboxamide, C(N)=O.
- C7 carries the ether oxygen.

**Linkers**
- The butene linker is N–CH2–CH=CH–CH2–N. The double bond is drawn with a defined geometry, and the chain goes down-right then down-left, which is consistent with trans (E). At the top, the CH2 attaches at about (453,330) and the alkene carbon at (400,395); at the bottom, the other alkene carbon is at about (405,465) and its CH2 at (355,525). The upper CH2 sits to the upper right and the lower CH2 to the lower left, which is the trans arrangement, so I wrote E.
- The ether chain is O–CH2–CH(N-piperidinyl)–CH2–O.

**Pyrazole**
- Ring atoms: N1(Et)–N2=C3(Me)–C4H=C5(C=O).
- SMILES fragment: CCn1nc(C)cc1C(=O)N...

**Top half**
Benzimidazole: n1c(NC(=O)pyrazole)n(CC=C...)c2c(OC...)cc(C(N)=O)cc12.

Full SMILES:
CCn1nc(C)cc1C(=O)Nc1nc2cc(C(N)=O)cc(OCC(N3CCCCC3)COc3cc(C(N)=O)cc4nc(NC(=O)c5cc(C)nn5CC)n(C/C=C/C5)c34)c2n1C5

I need to check the ring closure on this. The top benzimidazole N1 connects through the CH2 chain to the bottom N1, and the ring-closure digits must be distinct, so I rewrote it more carefully with the top unit as the start:

CCn1nc(C)cc1C(=O)Nc1nc2cc(C(N)=O)cc(OCC(N3CCCCC3)COc3cc(C(N)=O)cc4nc(NC(=O)c5cc(C)nn5CC)n(C/C=C/C6)c34)c2n1 would leave the chain unclosed.

The correct way is to close the linker with a ring-bond label:

CCn1nc(C)cc1C(=O)Nc1nc2cc(C(N)=O)cc(OCC(N3CCCCC3)COc3cc(C(N)=O)cc4nc(NC(=O)c5cc(C)nn5CC)n(C/C=C/C%10)c34)c2n1%10

Here the ring-bond label %10 opens at the CH2 and closes at the top N1. The final CH2 carries the label, so the closing bond joins it to the top N1. The top benzimidazole N1 is written "n1%10" at the end, and the earlier "n1" ring label was already closed on the pyrazole, so that reuse is valid.

This is a macrocyclic STING-agonist-type dimer: two identical benzimidazole units joined by a but-2-ene linker on one side and an O-CH2-CH(piperidinyl)-CH2-O linker on the other.

- The butene is N-CH2-CH=CH-CH2-N. The drawing shows a double bond in the ring-closing chain, and it is drawn in a cis-like zigzag (both CH2 on the same side?). The two CH2 groups run from the upper left and lower right, so they look trans. I will mark it E.
- The other linker is O-CH2-CH(N-piperidin-4-ol)-CH2-O.

**Top unit SMILES.** Ring atoms, in order:
- n1 (the N-butenyl nitrogen) is bonded to C2 (c(NC(=O)pyrazole)) and C7a.
- C2 is bonded to n3, then C3a, which leads to C4 (cH), C5 (c-CONH2), C6 (cH) and C7 (c-O).

Checking the closures:
- In the top unit, `n19` closes ring 1 (the imidazole) and ring 9 (the butene link).
- The bottom unit begins `c3cc(C(N)=O)cc4nc(NC(=O)...)n(C/C=C/C9)c34`. The O-bound carbon is c3, which also closes at c34 (the C7a carbon bonded to N1). Reading it out: c3 (C7, with O), cH, c(CONH2), cH, c4 (C3a), n, c(NHCO...), n(chain), c34 (C7a, closing to C7 and C3a). This is consistent.
- The butene in the top unit is `n19`, closed by `C9` from the bottom unit's `C/C=C/C9`, so the chain is N-CH2-CH=CH-CH2-N. This is correct.

text:
This is a STING agonist macrocycle of the kind found in the patent literature. I read it as two benzimidazole units joined by a butene linker on the N1 nitrogens and by a branched ether chain on the 7-oxygens.

**Top benzimidazole.** N1 carries the butenyl chain and C2 carries the NH–C(=O)–pyrazole group. N3 is the unsubstituted ring nitrogen. The carboxamide sits at C5 and the O-chain at C7.

**Pyrazole groups.** Each is 1-ethyl-3-methylpyrazole attached through its C5 to the carbonyl. In SMILES this is CCn1nc(C)cc1C(=O)N.

**Linker between the nitrogens.** N1(top)–CH2–CH=CH–CH2–N1(bottom). The double bond is drawn as cis or trans from the zigzag. The top CH2 goes down-left to a CH=, which then runs down to the next CH=, and then the CH2 goes down-left to the bottom N. This looks like a trans alkene, but the geometry is ambiguous, so I use the E form.

**Ether chain.** O(top)–CH2–CH(CH2CH2-morpholine)–CH2–O(bottom). The central CH carries a CH2CH2 chain ending at the morpholine N. It has no wedge, so no stereo is assigned.

**SMILES assembly.** The top benzimidazole is written as n1c(NC(=O)c2cc(C)nn2CC)n(C/C=C/C...)c3c(OC...)cc(C(N)=O)cc13. The macrocycle is closed with ring labels.

Top unit: `CCn1nc(C)cc1C(=O)Nc1nc2cc(C(N)=O)cc(OCC(CCN3CCOCC3)COc3cc(C(N)=O)cc4nc(NC(=O)c5cc(C)nn5CC)n(C/C=C/C5)c34)c2n1C5`

Checking the ring closures:
- Ring label 1 on the top benzimidazole (c1nc2...c2n1) closes at the last n1 before C5.
- The label 5 opens at the c5 of the second pyrazole, closes within that pyrazole (nn5), and is then reused for the linker. This is valid, since the first use closed before it was reopened.
- In `n(C/C=C/C5)c34`, the label 5 closes at the final `n1C5`, which bonds the CH2 to the top N1.
- Ring 3 is used by the morpholine and closed before `c3` is reused for the bottom benzene, so that is also fine.
- The top benzimidazole N1 is written as `n1C5` after `c2`, so its ring closure 1 matches the opening at the C2 carbon, and label 2 closes at c2.

**Pyrazole.** It is 1-ethyl-3-methylpyrazole-5-carbonyl: CCn1nc(C)cc1C(=O)N.

**Linker.** From the upper N1: CH2–CH=CH–CH2 to the lower N1. The alkene is drawn as a trans (E) double bond, because the chain continues on opposite sides. Reading the drawing, the upper CH2 goes down-left to the CH=, which then goes down to the next CH, and the lower CH2 goes down-left to N. That is a zigzag, so E.

**Ether bridge.** The upper C7–O–CH2–CH(N-piperidinyl)–CH2–O–C7' of the lower benzimidazole. The piperidine is 4-aminopiperidin-1-yl.

**SMILES construction.**

Upper benzimidazole: c1(NC(=O)c2cc(C)nn2CC)nc2cc(C(N)=O)cc(OCC(N3CCC(N)CC3)COc3cc(C(N)=O)cc4nc(NC(=O)c5cc(C)nn5CC)n(C/C=C/C...)c34)c2n1C/C=C/C...

Here ring label 5 is reused after closing the earlier pyrazole 5. The first pyrazole's 5 closes at "cc1" and the second at "nn5CC", so label 5 is free again when I open it at "C5" in the chain. The ring-closure partner is the last "C5" at the end, which is on the upper N1. The linker therefore reads: lower n–C/C=C/C(5), with the final C5 attached to the upper n1. Written out, the chain is n(C/C=C/C5) … n1C5. The upper n1 is bonded to C5, which is the CH2 closing to the chain's last CH2. This makes the chain N–CH2–CH=CH–CH2–N, which is correct.

Inside the aryl branch, the first piperidine uses 3 and closes it before 3 is reused. The spiro piperidine opens 3 and 4, and closes 3 with CC3 inside the spiro ring; 4 closes at C4. **Upper benzimidazole:** N1 carries the butenyl chain, C2 carries NHC(=O)-pyrazole, and N3 is the unsubstituted ring nitrogen. The benzene ring has the carboxamide at C5 and the O-CH2 at C7. The pyrazole is 1-ethyl-3-methyl-pyrazol-5-yl: CCn1nc(C)cc1C(=O)N.

**Butene linker:** N-CH2-CH=CH-CH2-N. The double bond is drawn as a plain zigzag, but it sits in a ring and the geometry looks like E. The upper CH2 goes down to the CH=, which then goes down-left to the next CH=, and then to CH2 and the lower N. I will assign E (trans), though the drawing is ambiguous.

**SMILES construction:**

Upper unit: CCn1nc(C)cc1C(=O)Nc1nc2cc(C(N)=O)cc(OCC(N3CCC(OP(=O)(O)O)CC3)COc3cc(C(N)=O)cc4nc(NC(=O)c5cc(C)nn5CC)n(c34)C/C=C/C2...

The ring closure is awkward to write this way, so I use explicit ring labels instead.

Upper benzimidazole: n1(CC=CC...)c(NC(=O)pyrazole)nc2cc(C(N)=O)cc(O...)c12

Full SMILES:
CCn1nc(C)cc1C(=O)Nc1nc2cc(C(N)=O)cc3c2n1C/C=C/Cn1c(NC(=O)c2cc(C)nn2CC)nc2cc(C(N)=O)cc(c21)OCC(CO3)N1CCC(OP(=O)(O)O)CC1

Check of the closures:
- The first benzimidazole has c2 (C3a), then cc(C(N)=O)c, then c3 (C7, which bears O3), then c2 (C7a) closing the ring, then n1 (N1) closing to C2. This is correct, and N1 bears the CH2.
- The second benzimidazole starts at n1 (new label 1, reused after closure), then c(NC(=O)...) is C2, then n is N3, then c2 is C3a, then cc(C(N)=O)c is C4, C5, C6, then c(...) is C7 with the substituent OCC..., and c21 is C7a closing to both C3a and N1. The ring-closure digits work out.
- The C7 of the second unit carries O-CH2-CH(N)-CH2-O3, which closes to the first unit's C7. This is correct.

SMILES: CCn1nc(C)cc1C(=O)Nc1nc2cc(C(N)=O)cc3c2n1C/C=C/Cn1c(NC(=O)c2cc(C)nn2CC)nc2cc(C(N)=O)cc(c21)OCC(CO3)N1CCC(OP(=O)(O)O)CC1

I checked them against the standard VH032 configuration and assumed the drawing matches it. I did not independently confirm the hash/wedge directions in the image.

1. **Top aryl acetamide:** a 4-(trifluoromethoxy)phenyl-CH2-C(=O) group is acylating the piperidine nitrogen.
2. **Piperidine core:** C3 carries a hashed F (away from the viewer) and C4 carries a wedged O (toward the viewer). I worked out the chirality of each centre from the drawn geometry. The SMILES order is N1–C2–C3(F)–C4(O)–C5–C6, and both stereocentres come out as `@@`.
3. **Benzamide and linker:**

   - The imidazole N1 carries a three-carbon chain (CH2CH2CH2) ending in C(=O)NH.
   - That amide NH is followed by a seven-carbon chain (counted along the zigzag) ending in NH.
4. **Pomalidomide end:** the terminal NH is attached to the 4-position of the isoindoline-1,3-dione, whose nitrogen bears the 2,6-dioxopiperidin-3-yl ring. That ring's stereocentre is drawn with plain bonds, so it has no stereo label.

name: rb_0506
text:
Reading the structure region by region:

**Right side, thieno[3,2-c]pyridinone core.**
- The thiophene ring is S, C2 (bearing the carboxamide), C3 (CH), C3a and C7a.
- The fused pyridinone ring continues from C3a to C4 (=O), then N5 (methyl), C6 (CH), and C7, which carries the aryl group and bonds to C7a.
- SMILES for the core: c1(C(=O)N...)cc2c(s1)c(Ar)cn(C)c2=O

- It is a phenyl ring bearing two OMe groups and a CH2N(CH3)2 group between them, so it is 3,5-dimethoxy-4-(dimethylaminomethyl)phenyl.
- SMILES: c1(OC)cc(...)cc(OC)c1CN(C)C

**Amide and piperidine.**
- The amide NH attaches to C4 of a piperidine.
- C3 of that piperidine carries two fluorines (CF2), next to C2, which bonds to the ring N.
- The piperidine N attaches to the isoindolinone.
- SMILES: NC1CCN(Ar)CC1(F)F

**Isoindolinone.**

- The C=O is on the carbon attached to the aromatic ring carbon adjacent to the one bearing the piperidine N, so the piperidine sits at position 5 of the isoindolinone.
- Aromatic ring: c1 (C=O side, C7a), then CH (C7), then C6 bearing the piperidine N, then CH, CH, and finally C3a bearing the CH2.
- In the drawing, the C=O-bearing carbon connects to a CH, which connects to the C–N(piperidine) carbon. That carbon then goes to a CH, a CH, and the CH2-bearing carbon.

name: rb_0503
text:
I read the drawing as a cyclic heptapeptide, working from the N-terminus around the ring.

**Sequence.** The chain is Ac‑Nle‑Glu(side chain)‑Met(O2)‑Nal‑Arg‑Trp, closed through a diamine linker.
- The N-terminus is an acetyl group on a norleucine (n‑butyl side chain).
- Next is a glutamic acid whose side-chain carboxyl forms an amide with the linker.
- Next is a methionine sulfone (CH2CH2–SO2–CH3).
- Next is a 1‑naphthylalanine.
- Next is an arginine with a guanidine side chain.
- Last is a tryptophan whose C=O is bonded to the other end of the linker.

**Linker.** The line from the Glu side-chain amide NH to the Trp C(=O)–NH has five CH2 carbons by my count. I took it as pentane‑1,5‑diyl; this is the least certain count in the drawing.

**Stereochemistry** (assigned from the wedges and hashes at each α‑carbon):
- Nle is R, so D.
- Glu is S, so L.
- Met sulfone is S, so L.
- 1‑Nal is R, so D.
- Arg is S, so L.
- Trp is S, so L.

I wrote the SMILES with a ring-closure digit 1 joining the Glu α‑carbon to the Met C(=O)–N end, and checked the @/@@ marks against these assignments.

name: rb_0507
text:
I read the molecule as a 9-aryl-3,6-bis(dimethylamino)acridine in its 10H, iminium-quinoid form, carrying a benzoate that is substituted with a diaza-crown ether.

**Acridine part**
- The upper-left ring is aromatic and carries an NMe2 group.
- The central ring has an NH at position 10, and C9 is double-bonded to the right-hand ring.
- The right-hand ring is quinoid: C3 is double-bonded to N⁺Me2, and the ring double bonds are C1=C2 and C4=C4a.
- I wrote this ring in Kekulé form because it has exocyclic double bonds.

**Benzoate ring**
- C1 is bonded to C9 of the acridine.
- Its ortho neighbour C2 carries the carboxylate, C(=O)[O⁻].
- C3 is a plain CH.
- C4 carries OMe.
- C5 carries the crown-ether nitrogen.
- C6 is a plain CH.

**Crown ether**
- It is a 1,4,10-trioxa-7,13-diaza macrocycle.
- Starting from the nitrogen on the benzoate, the ring runs N–CH2CH2–O–CH2CH2–O–CH2CH2–N(2-methoxyphenyl)–CH2CH2–O–CH2CH2 back to the first nitrogen.
- The second nitrogen carries a 2-methoxyphenyl group.

No wedges, hashes or cis/trans geometry are drawn, so the SMILES has no stereo marks.

name: rb_0508
text:
I read the drawing as a 15-membered macrocycle built from three amino-acid-derived units and a diaryl sulfide linker.

**Fragments**
- **Tryptophan unit:** the indole nitrogen carries a Boc group. The α-nitrogen is N-methylated and its carbonyl is bonded to an NH–CH2 group on the benzene ring.
- **Benzene ring:** the ring carbon bearing CH2 is next to C–Br. Going round the ring, the next two carbons are CH, then CH, then C–Cl, and finally the carbon bearing S.
- **Sulfur bridge:** S joins the benzene ring to C2 of a pyridine. The pyridine C3 carries CH2–NH, and that NH is bonded to the α-carbon of the first ornithine.
- **First ornithine unit:** its side chain is (CH2)3–NH–Boc. Its carbonyl forms an amide with the NH of the second ornithine.
- **Second ornithine unit:** its side chain is also (CH2)3–NH–Boc. Its carbonyl forms an amide with the N-methyl nitrogen of the tryptophan unit, closing the ring.

**Stereochemistry (all three centres are wedged, and each works out as S)**
- Tryptophan α-carbon: the CH2 wedge points to the viewer and the neighbours N, C=O, CH2 run counterclockwise, giving S.
- Second ornithine α-carbon: the same assignment gives S.
- First ornithine α-carbon: the same assignment gives S.
- Written in SMILES, these are `[C@@H]` for the tryptophan and first-ornithine centres and `[C@H]` for the second-ornithine centre. The second one differs because its ring-closure digit changes the neighbour order.

I checked the SMILES atom by atom against the drawing.

text:
I read the molecule as a macrocycle built from Dab, Lys, and N-methyl-Trp residues, closed through a pyridyl-thio-aryl linker.

**Residues and linker**
- **Dab:** H2N‑CH2CH2‑CH(α‑C) with the α‑NH linked through a CH2 to C3 of the pyridine. Its C=O is amide-bonded to the Lys NH.
- **Lys:** The side chain is (CH2)4NH2. Its C=O is bonded to the N‑methyl nitrogen of Trp.
- **N‑Me‑Trp:** The side chain is CH2‑indol‑3‑yl. Its C=O is bonded to an NH, which connects through a CH2 to the central benzene ring.
- **Central benzene ring:** Going round the ring, the substituents are S (to pyridine C2), then CH2NH, then the aryl group, then two CH, then Cl. The Cl-bearing carbon sits next to the S-bearing carbon.
- **Aryl group:** A 4-carboxy-3-hydroxyphenyl, i.e. the salicylic acid part.

**Stereochemistry**
The three α‑carbons carry wedges. Working out CIP priorities from the drawing, all three come out S, the L-configuration. I then converted this to SMILES `@`/`@@` using the neighbour order in the string.

**Ring-closure digits**
The Trp indole uses digits 4 and 5 so they do not clash with the benzene ring that is still open at that point.

I read the structure as a macrocyclic bis-benzimidazole. Two identical benzimidazole units are joined by a but-2-enyl linker between their ring nitrogens and by a bridging 2-aminopropane-1,3-diyl bis-ether.

- **Pyrazole amide caps:** each benzimidazole C2 carries an NH–C(=O) link to a 1-ethyl-3-methylpyrazol-5-yl group.
- **Benzimidazole core:** each core has a primary carboxamide at C5 and an ether oxygen at C7.
- **Linker:** the N1 atoms of the two benzimidazoles are joined by CH2–CH=CH–CH2. The two CH2 groups lie on opposite sides of the double bond in the drawing, so I assigned E.
- **Bridge:** the two C7 oxygens connect through OCH2–CH–CH2O. The central CH bears the nitrogen of a pyrrolidine-3-carboxylic acid. It is a stereocentre by connectivity but drawn with plain bonds, so I gave it no stereo label. The pyrrolidine C3 is likewise unlabelled.

I checked the SMILES for valid ring closures and atom counts against the drawing.

SMILES: CCn1nc(C)cc1C(=O)Nc1nc2cc(C(N)=O)cc3c2n1C/C=C/Cn1c(NC(=O)c2cc(C)nn2CC)nc2cc(C(N)=O)cc(c12)OCC(CO3)N1CCC(C1)C(=O)O

name: rb_0527
text:
I read the structure in four parts and then assembled them.

- **Left benzene ring:** it carries the nitrile. Its two neighbouring ring carbons carry a CH2CH2–O chain and a CH2–O chain.
- **Macrocycle:**
  - The CH2CH2–O chain ends in an ether O that bonds through a CH2 to the central benzene.
  - The CH2–O chain ends in an O on C2 of the pyridine.
  - Pyridine C6 is bonded to the central benzene, meta to the carbon bearing the CH2–O.
- **Central benzene:** the carbon ortho to the CH2–O carbon carries a CH2 that links to C2 of the benzimidazole.
- **Benzimidazole:**
  - N1 carries a CH2 attached to an oxetan-2-yl group.
  - C4 carries OCH2CH2OCH3.
  - C6 carries CO2Me.

The only stereocentre drawn with a hashed bond is oxetane C2. I took the hashed CH2–N bond as pointing behind the plane, which puts H toward the viewer. The CIP priorities are O > CH2N > ring CH2 > H. Tracing O → CH2N → ring CH2 on the drawing gives clockwise, and reversing for the H toward the viewer gives counterclockwise, so the centre is S. In the SMILES, the neighbour order CH2N, H, O, CH2 makes `@@` the S form.

I checked that the ring-closure digits pair up correctly and that each atom's connectivity matches the drawing.

SMILES: N#Cc1ccc2c(c1)CCOCc1cc(ccc1Cc1nc3c(OCCOC)cc(C(=O)OC)cc3n1C[C@@H]1CCO1)-c1cccc(n1)OC2

name: rb_0531
text:
I read the drawing region by region and assembled the SMILES from the pieces below.

**Macrocycle, going around the ring**
- **Ornithine residue:** H2N–CH2CH2CH2 side chain (three CH2 groups) on the alpha carbon, which carries a wedge bond to the chain. Its ring NH is bonded to a CH2 on the pyridine, and its C=O is bonded to the lysine NH.
- **Lysine residue:** a four-CH2 side chain ending in NH2, and an alpha carbon drawn with a wedge. Its C=O is bonded to the N-methyl nitrogen of the next residue.
- **N-methyl tryptophan residue:** N(CH3), then an alpha carbon with a wedged CH2 to indol-3-yl (the indole NH is drawn). Its C=O is bonded to an NH, which is bonded to a CH2 on the central benzene ring.
- **Central benzene ring:**
  - one carbon carries the CH2–NH;
  - the adjacent carbon carries the S bridge;
  - the next carbon carries Cl;
  - the fourth ring carbon is CH;
  - the fifth ring carbon is CH;
  - the sixth carbon, adjacent to the CH2-bearing carbon, carries the pyridyl group.
- **S-linked pyridine:** a 2-pyridyl whose C3 carries the CH2–NH of the ornithine.
- **Aryl substituent:** a pyridine bonded through its C5 and carrying COOH at C2 (a picolinic acid).

**Stereochemistry**
The CORN rule applied to the wedges shows all three alpha carbons have the L configuration. This gives @@ for the ornithine carbon as written in the SMILES, and @ for the lysine and tryptophan carbons.

SMILES: NCCC[C@@H]1NCc2cccnc2Sc2c(CNC(=O)[C@H](Cc3c[nH]c4ccccc34)N(C)C(=O)[C@H](CCCCN)NC1=O)c(-c1ccc(C(=O)O)nc1)ccc2Cl

name: rb_0535
text:
This looks like a STING agonist dimer: two benzimidazole units joined by a but-2-enyl linker on N1 of each and by a 2-(pyridin-2-yl)propane-1,3-diyl bis-ether on the 7-oxygens.

**Pieces read from the drawing**
- Each pyrazole is 1-ethyl-3-methylpyrazole-5-carbonyl: CCn1nc(C)cc1C(=O)N.
- Each benzimidazole has the 2-NH-acyl group, N1 bearing the butenyl chain, a 7-O ether and a 5-carboxamide.
- The central linker is O-CH2-CH(2-pyridyl)-CH2-O.
- The double bond in the butenyl linker is drawn without clear cis/trans geometry, so I left it unspecified (the drawing looks roughly trans, but I did not assign it).

**Top benzimidazole**
N1 is attached to the CH2 of the butenyl chain. C2 carries the NHC(=O)pyrazole. N3 is the "N" at the top. C3a–C4(H)–C5(CONH2)–C6(H)–C7(O)–C7a.
SMILES: n1c(NC(=O)c2cc(C)nn2CC)n(CC=CC...)c3c(OC...)cc(C(N)=O)cc13

**Full SMILES**
CCn1nc(C)cc1C(=O)Nc1nc2cc(C(N)=O)cc(OCC(c3ccccn3)COc3cc(C(N)=O)cc4nc(NC(=O)c5cc(C)nn5CC)n(CC=CC5)c34)c2n1CC=C... 

That draft has a ring-closure problem, so I rebuilt it with the butenyl chain closed explicitly.

Top unit: `CCn1nc(C)cc1C(=O)Nc1nc2cc(C(N)=O)cc(OCC(c3ccccn3)COc3cc(C(N)=O)cc4nc(NC(=O)c5cc(C)nn5CC)n(c34)C/C=C/C...` is also messy, so I used ring-closure digit 9 to carry the butenyl chain from the top N1 to the bottom N1.

Top unit: `CCn1nc(C)cc1C(=O)Nc1nc2cc(C(N)=O)cc(OCC(c3ccccn3)COc3cc(C(N)=O)cc4nc(NC(=O)c5cc(C)nn5CC)n(CC=C9)c34)c2n19`

This still has a malformed closure, so I wrote it out with the chain as an explicit atom sequence. In this version the top N1 is the last atom of the first unit, followed by CC=CC to the bottom N1, and the bottom unit is written inside a branch:

CCn1nc(C)cc1C(=O)Nc1nc2cc(C(N)=O)cc(OCC(c3ccccn3)COc3cc(C(N)=O)cc4nc(NC(=O)c5cc(C)nn5CC)n(CC=CC)c34)c2n1CC=CC

That branch sequence is wrong because the chain must connect the two N atoms. The correct connection uses ring-closure label 9 on both N1 atoms, with the chain written once:

CCn1nc(C)cc1C(=O)Nc1nc2cc(C(N)=O)cc(OCC(c3ccccn3)COc3cc(C(N)=O)cc4nc(NC(=O)c5cc(C)nn5CC)n(C/C=C/C9)c34)c2n19

I did not fully resolve this last string. Written this way the chain is only CH2-CH=CH-CH2 and its final CH2 closes onto the top N1 through label 9. This is the intended connectivity, with the double bond geometry left unspecified.

SMILES: CCn1nc(C)cc1C(=O)Nc1nc2cc(C(N)=O)cc(OCC(c3ccccn3)COc3cc(C(N)=O)cc4nc(NC(=O)c5cc(C)nn5CC)n(CC=CC9)c34)c2n19

name: rb_0534
text:
I read the molecule as a macrocycle built from two identical benzimidazole units joined by two linkers.

- **Benzimidazole units:** each has a primary carboxamide (C(=O)NH2) on the benzene ring and an NH–C(=O)– link at C2 to a 1-ethyl-3-methylpyrazol-5-yl group. Each also carries an aryl ether oxygen at C7, next to the N1 that bears the butenyl chain.
- **Butenyl linker:** N1–CH2–CH=CH–CH2–N1′ joins the two benzimidazole nitrogens. From the drawn coordinates the two CH2 substituents lie on opposite sides of the double bond, so I assigned E (trans).
- **Ether linker:** each C7 oxygen leads to a CH2, and the two CH2 groups meet at a central CH. This CH carries the nitrogen of a 3-oxa-8-azabicyclo[3.2.1]octane, whose bridges are CH2–O–CH2 and CH2–CH2.
- **Stereochemistry:** the central CH and the two bicycle bridgeheads have no wedges or hashes in the drawing, so I left them unspecified. Only the E double bond is marked.

I checked the ring closures by hand: the pyrazole, both benzimidazole systems, the bicycle, and the macrocycle closure at the top ether oxygen (label %10).

SMILES: NC(=O)c1cc2nc(NC(=O)c3cc(C)nn3CC)n(C/C=C/Cn3c(NC(=O)c4cc(C)nn4CC)nc4cc(C(N)=O)cc(OCC(N5C6CCC5COC6)CO%10)c34)c2c(O%10)c1

name: rb_0536
text:

- **Left kinase-binding unit:** an imidazo[1,2-a]pyrazine carrying a cyclopropyl group on the pyrazine ring and a 1H-pyrazol-4-yl group on the imidazole ring. At C8 it has an NH link to a 2-fluorophenyl ring, which carries a para C(=O) group.
- **Linker:** that carbonyl forms an amide with a piperazine nitrogen. The other piperazine nitrogen is attached through CH2C(=O)NH to a triethylene-glycol-type chain (NCCOCCOCCOCC(=O)), which ends in an amide to the next unit.
- **Right-hand VHL ligand:** an L-tert-leucine (the wedge on the NH-bearing carbon) coupled to 4-hydroxyproline. The hydroxyproline has the standard (2S,4R) configuration, which matches the wedge and hash bonds in the drawing. Its carboxyl forms an amide with 4-(4-methylthiazol-5-yl)benzylamine.
- **Stereochemistry:** I wrote the stereocentres in the standard VH032 form and checked the tert-leucine centre against its neighbour order. The proline centres are copied from the standard VH032 SMILES rather than re-derived from the wedges.

name: rb_0537
text:
I read the molecule as a macrocycle fused to a benzimidazole ester, and built the SMILES in four parts.

**Macrocycle**
- The left benzene ring carries Cl and F. It is linked through a CH2CH2–O–CH2 bridge to the central benzene ring.
- The same left ring is also linked through a CH2–O bridge to the 2-position of a pyridine.
- The 6-position of the pyridine is bonded directly to the central benzene ring.
- The central benzene ring carries one F, one CH2 that connects to the benzimidazole, and the pyridyl and ether-bridge attachments. Its six ring positions, in order, are: ether CH2, CH, pyridyl, C–F, CH, CH2-benzimidazole.

**Benzimidazole**
- C2 bears the CH2 that connects to the central ring.
- N1 carries a CH2 group attached to an oxetan-2-yl ring.
- Ring carbon 4 (next to the N3 side) carries OCH2CH2OMe.
- Ring carbon 6 carries CO2Me.

**Stereochemistry**
- The only drawn stereocentre is the oxetane C2, which has a hashed bond to the CH2N group.
- The CIP priorities are O > CH2N > ring CH2 > H.
- With the hashed CH2N pointing back and H implicitly toward the viewer, the O → CH2N → CH2 sequence looks clockwise from the front. Because H points toward the viewer, the true configuration is S.
- In the SMILES written as `n1C[C@@H]1CCO1`, `@@` encodes S for this neighbour order.

SMILES: Clc1cc2CCOCc3cc(-c4cccc(OCc2c(F)c1)n4)c(F)cc3Cc1nc3c(OCCOC)cc(C(=O)OC)cc3n1C[C@@H]1CCO1

text:

name: rb_0538
text:
I read the molecule as a PROTAC-type compound, built from three parts joined by an amide linker.

- **Left part:** a pyridine with a 3-carboxamide and a 2-O-linked piperidine, and an imidazole at the 5-position. The piperidine bears a 3-fluoro, a 4-oxy and an N-acyl group, the acyl being 4-(trifluoromethoxy)phenylacetyl. From the wedge and hash bonds I assigned both piperidine stereocentres as R (the F and O are trans).
- **Linker:** the imidazole N1 carries a butyl chain, then NH–C(=O)CH2CH2–O–CH2CH2–C(=O)–NH.
- **Right part:** a VHL-type ligand, namely tert-leucine, then (2S,4R)-4-hydroxyproline, then an amide to 4-(4-methylthiazol-5-yl)benzylamine. I took its stereochemistry from the standard VHL ligand, which the drawing matches.

I checked the stereo tags by working out the CIP priorities for the two piperidine centres. For the tert-leucine and hydroxyproline centres I converted the known VHL-ligand SMILES to the atom order used in my string.

- **Aryl acetamide:** the 4-(trifluoromethoxy)phenyl group is attached through CH2–C(=O) to the piperidine nitrogen.
- **Piperidine:** it carries F at C3, drawn with a hashed bond, and the ether oxygen at C4, drawn with a wedge. From the 2D geometry I assigned C3 as `[C@@H](F)` and C4 as `[C@H](O…)`, with the SMILES written in the order N–C2–C3–C4.
- **Pyridine core:** the ring has O-linked piperidine at C2, a primary carboxamide at C3, and the imidazole at C5.

- **Thalidomide-type end:** the NH sits at the 4-position of the isoindoline-1,3-dione, whose nitrogen is attached to the 2,6-dioxopiperidin-3-yl ring. That carbon has plain bonds, so it has no stereo label.

name: rb_0533
text:
I read this as a rifamycin-derived benzoxazino (phenoxazine-fused) ansamycin and built the SMILES region by region.

- **Chromophore:** a naphthofuranone core with a quinone carbonyl and a phenolic OH, fused to a phenoxazine ring. The phenoxazine ring carries a free OH and an OCH2CH2NHAc substituent. The amide NH sits on the quinone ring.
- **Ansa chain:** starting from the amide carbonyl, the chain runs C(Me)=CH–CH=CH (the C(Me)=CH double bond is Z, the other E), then CH(Me), CH(OH), CH(Me), CH(OH), CH(Me), CH(OAc), CH(Me), CH(OMe), CH=CH–O (E enol ether). The enol-ether oxygen is attached to the quaternary carbon of the furanone, which also carries a methyl group.
- **Stereochemistry:** I took the chain stereocentres from the usual natural rifamycin configuration, which matches the drawing pattern but is recalled from memory rather than re-derived from every wedge. The quaternary furanone carbon I assigned from the drawn wedges (methyl hashed, chain oxygen bold). The double-bond geometries follow the drawing.
- **Check:** ring closures and parentheses balance, and the ring closures reproduce the quinone, benzene, furanone and phenoxazine rings. I did not run it through a parser.

name: rb_0542
text:
I read this as an Ac‑Nle cyclic hexapeptide: Ac‑Nle‑cyclo[Asp‑His‑(3,4‑Cl2)Phe‑Arg‑Trp‑linker]. The Asp side‑chain carbonyl is joined through an amide to a five‑carbon diamine chain, (CH2)5. That chain's other nitrogen is acylated by the Trp carbonyl, which closes the ring.

Points I read from the drawing:
- **Chain length:** I counted five CH2 groups between the two amide nitrogens. The zigzag is slightly ambiguous, so this is my best reading.
- **Stereochemistry:** I assumed L‑configuration at Nle, Asp, His, Arg and Trp. I took the Phe(3,4‑Cl2) as D, because it has a clear wedge. I did not check the hashed and wedged bonds on the other residues one by one.
- **Substituents:** the Nle side chain is n‑butyl and the N‑terminus is acetylated. His is drawn as an imidazole and Trp as an indole. Arg carries a guanidine, and the Phe ring has chlorines at the 3 and 4 positions.

name: rb_0545
text:
The drawing shows a PROTAC-type molecule with formic acid as a separate component. I read it region by region.

**Aryl group.** The ring carries two OMe groups and a CH2N(CH3)2 group between them. It attaches to the core at the position para to the CH2NMe2 group.

**Core.** This is a thieno[3,2-c]pyridin-4-one. The pyridone ring has N-methyl, a C=O, and C7 bearing the aryl group. The thiophene ring has S, and its C2 carries the NH.

Core SMILES: O=C1N(C)C=C(Ar)c2sc(NC(=O)...)cc12. In the drawing, C7 bonds to C7a, which bonds to S. C3a bonds to C4 (C=O). The thiophene C3 is the CH, and C2 carries the NH.

**Linker.** NH–C(=O)–piperidin-4-yl, with the piperidine N acylated by C(=O)CCCCO–. Counting the chain from the carbonyl: C(=O), then CH2, CH2, CH2, CH2, then O. The drawing shows the carbonyl carbon followed by four vertices before O, so this is a 5-aryloxypentanoyl group: C(=O)CCCCO.

**Thalidomide end.** The O is attached at position 4 of the isoindoline-1,3-dione. The N is attached to the 2,6-dioxopiperidin-3-yl group. The stereocentre is drawn with plain bonds, so no stereo is given.

**Assembly.**

- Aryl: c1(OC)cc(cc(OC)c1CN(C)C)
- Core: Cn1cc(Ar)c2sc(NC(=O)C3CCN(CC3)C(=O)CCCCOc3cccc4C(=O)N(C5CCC(=O)NC5=O)C(=O)c34)cc2c1=O
- Formic acid: OC=O

SMILES: Cn1cc(-c2cc(OC)c(CN(C)C)c(OC)c2)c2sc(NC(=O)C3CCN(CC3)C(=O)CCCCOc3cccc4C(=O)N(C5CCC(=O)NC5=O)C(=O)c34)cc2c1=O.OC=O

name: rb_0547
text:
I read the structure as a macrocycle built from three parts, then wrote the SMILES from that reading.

**1,4-Diazepane.** The seven-membered ring is N–CH2–CH2–CH2–N–CH2–CH2, with the two nitrogens separated by three carbons on one side and two on the other.

**Macrocycle links:**
- From the left nitrogen, three CH2 groups lead to the ester O, which connects to the upper aryl C=O.
- From the lower nitrogen, two CH2 groups lead to a CH.
- That CH carries an O–C(=O)–aryl ester.
- From the same CH, three CH2 groups lead to the aryl ether O on the upper ring.

**Lower aryl ring.** It is a 3,4-dimethoxy-5-benzyloxy benzoate, attached through its C=O to the CH oxygen.

The CH carbon is a stereocentre by connectivity, but it is drawn with plain bonds, so I gave it no stereo marking.

I checked ring closures and counts: the diazepane closes as a seven-membered ring, and the upper aryl ring closes correctly with the ester carbon on a carbon flanked by two ring CH atoms.

name: rb_0546
text:
I read the structure as a macrocyclic benzonitrile–benzene–pyridine core joined through a CH2 linker to a substituted benzimidazole carboxylic acid.

**Macrocycle**
- The benzonitrile ring carries a CH2CH2–O–CH2 bridge to the central benzene ring.
- The same ring also carries a CH2–O bridge to the pyridine 6-position.
- The central benzene ring has three substituents: the CH2–O bridge, the pyridine at the position meta to it, and the CH2 linker to the benzimidazole, which sits ortho to the bridge carbon.
- The pyridine has the ring N next to the aryl-bearing carbon, and the F at the 3-position.

**Benzimidazole**
- C2 bears the CH2 linker to the central benzene ring.
- N1 bears CH2 attached to oxetan-2-yl.
- C4 bears OCH2CH2OCH3.
- C6 bears CO2H.

**Stereochemistry**
- The oxetane C2 is the only stereocentre.
- I took the bond to the oxetane as a stereo bond and assigned it S, which is the configuration in the closely related compound danuglipron. I could not confirm it from the drawing alone.
- The CIP priorities at that carbon are O > CH2N > ring CH2 > H, and `C[C@@H]1CCO1` written with the CH2N carbon first gives S.

I checked the ring closures and atom counts of the SMILES against the drawing.

SMILES: N#Cc1ccc2c(c1)CCOCc1cc(ccc1Cc1nc3c(OCCOC)cc(C(=O)O)cc3n1C[C@@H]1CCO1)-c1nc(OC2)ccc1F

name: rb_0541
text:
This is a symmetric dimer: two identical bicyclic thiazepine–pyrrolidine units, each carrying an N‑methylalanine amide, joined through a 2‑aminoindanyl ether to a hexa‑2,4‑diyne‑1,6‑diyl linker. I read one half and wrote it out, then wrote the other half with the same stereodescriptors.

**One half, read from the drawing**
- **Alanine unit:** CH3‑NH‑CH(CH3)‑C(=O)‑NH‑, with the methyl hashed. This is L‑Ala (S).
- **Thiazepine ring:** seven‑membered, containing S, CH2, CH2, CH(NH‑acyl), C(=O), N and the ring‑fusion CH. The CH bearing NH is S (wedged CH2). The ring‑fusion CH, with hashed H next to S, is S.
- **Pyrrolidine ring:** shares the N and the ring‑fusion CH, and also contains a CH2, a spiro carbon and the CH carrying the carboxamide (wedged), which is S.
- **Spiro ring:** a cyclopent‑3‑ene. The spiro carbon is not a stereocentre because both ring paths are identical.
- **Amide and indane:** the carboxamide NH is bonded to C1 of an indane. C1 (hashed N) is S and C2 (hashed O) is R, so the two substituents are trans.
- **Linker:** the indane C2 oxygen continues as O‑CH2‑C≡C‑C≡C‑CH2‑O to the second, identical half.

I assigned each @/@@ tag by working out the CIP descriptor from the drawn wedges and hashes. I did not run the SMILES through a parser, so the check is by hand: atom counts, ring closures and tags are consistent with the drawing.

name: rb_0549
text:
The SMILES below was read region by region from the drawing.

- **Left heterocycle:** an imidazo[1,2-a]pyrazine carrying a cyclopropyl on the pyrazine carbon, a 1H-pyrazol-4-yl on the imidazole carbon next to the bridgehead nitrogen, and an NH link at C8.
- **Aryl amide:** the NH connects to a 2-fluoro-4-carbonylphenyl ring, and the carbonyl forms an amide with one nitrogen of a piperazine.
- **Linker:** the other piperazine nitrogen carries CH2C(=O)NH, followed by a chain of six CH2 groups ending in an aryl ether oxygen.
- **Right aryl ring:** the oxygen sits on a benzene ring that has a CH2NH group ortho to the oxygen and a 4-methylthiazol-5-yl group para to the CH2.
- **VHL-type end:** the CH2NH is acylated by a hydroxyproline unit, drawn as the 4-hydroxy-pyrrolidine-2-carboxamide with one wedge and one hash. Its ring nitrogen is acylated by tert-leucine, whose NH carries a 1-fluorocyclopropanecarbonyl group.
- **Stereochemistry:** I took the three stereocentres from the standard VHL ligand (VH032-type) SMILES, where the hydroxyproline is (2S,4R) and the tert-leucine is (S). I matched this to the drawn wedges and hashes by recall of that standard form, not by working out each centre from the image.

name: rb_0548
text:
I read this as an N-acetylated cyclic peptide: Ac-Nle-cyclo[Glu-His-D-Phe(2-Me)-Arg-Trp] closed through a 1,4-diaminobutane linker. The Glu side-chain amide connects through NH-(CH2)4-NH to the Trp C-terminal carbonyl.

Reading by region:
- **N-terminus:** acetyl on norleucine (n-butyl side chain), with the butyl bond hashed.
- **Glu:** the γ-carboxyl is the macrocycle amide, with the side chain on a wedge.
- **His:** imidazole attached at its 4-position through CH2, hashed.
- **Phe:** 2-methylbenzyl side chain on a wedge.
- **Arg:** a three-carbon chain ending in a guanidine, hashed.
- **Trp:** indol-3-ylmethyl side chain, hashed.

Stereochemistry from the wedges and hashes: Nle, Glu, His, Arg and Trp come out L. The 2-methyl-Phe comes out D. In the SMILES, residues written from the carbonyl side use `[C@H]` for L and `[C@@H]` for D.

name: rb_0551
text:
I read the molecule as a PROTAC-style conjugate with three parts joined by a linker.

**Left warhead.** The core is an imidazo[1,2-a]pyrazine with a cyclopropyl at C6 and a 1H-pyrazol-4-yl at C3. Its C8 carries an NH link to a phenyl ring that bears fluorine ortho to the NH and a carbonyl para to it.

**Linker.** The aryl carbonyl forms an amide with a piperazine nitrogen. The other piperazine nitrogen carries CH2C(=O)NH, followed by six CH2 groups (counted vertex by vertex along the zigzag), then C(=O)NH.

**Right side (VHL-type ligand).** The linker amide NH is attached to a tert-leucine residue, CH(tBu)C(=O). That carbonyl acylates the nitrogen of a 4-hydroxypyrrolidine-2-carboxamide. The carboxamide NH is attached to a CH(CH3) group on a para-phenylene ring, which carries a 4-methylthiazol-5-yl group.

**Stereochemistry.** I assigned the stereocentres by matching the drawn wedges and hashes to the usual VHL-ligand configuration (S-tert-leucine, 2S,4R-hydroxyproline, S-1-arylethyl). I did not check each wedge independently against the SMILES chirality tags, so this is a best match rather than a verified read.

name: rb_0554
text:
This is a PROTAC-type molecule. I read it in sections from left to right.

**Left aryl group.** The benzene ring carries a CH2N(CH3)2 group at the position between two OMe groups. The ring attaches to the thienopyridinone at the position para to the CH2NMe2 carbon. SMILES for this fragment: c1(OC)c(CN(C)C)c(OC)cc(c1)-

**Thieno[3,2-c]pyridin-4-one core.**
- The thiophene S is bonded to C2, which carries the carboxamide, and to C7a.
- C7a is bonded to C7, which carries the aryl group.
- C7 is bonded to C6H, which is bonded to N5(CH3).
- N5 is bonded to C4(=O), which is bonded to C3a, and C3a to C3H.
- C3H is double-bonded to C2.

SMILES for the core: c1(-Ar)c2sc(C(=O)N...)cc2c(=O)n(C)c1. Written with explicit ring closures: O=C1N(C)C=C(Ar)C2=C1C=C(C(=O)N...)S2.

**Amide and spiro linker.** The amide N is bonded to a cyclobutane CH. The cyclobutane has a spiro carbon that is also part of a piperidine ring, so this is a 7-azaspiro[3.5]nonane. The cyclobutane CH is bonded to two CH2 groups, and both CH2 groups are bonded to the spiro carbon.
- Fragment: NC1CC2(C1)CCN(CC2)C(=O)...

**Chain to the piperazine.** The piperidine N is acylated: C(=O)CCN3CCN(CC3)-Ar.

**Isoindoline-dione.** The piperazine N is bonded to the aryl ring of the isoindoline-1,3-dione, at the 5-position. The isoindoline N is bonded to the 2,6-dioxopiperidin-3-yl group.
- Fragment: c1ccc2c(c1)C(=O)N(C3CCC(=O)NC3=O)C2=O

**Full SMILES:**
CN(C)Cc1c(OC)cc(cc1OC)C1=CN(C)C(=O)C2=C1SC(=C2)C(=O)NC1CC2(C1)CCN(CC2)C(=O)CCN1CCN(CC1)c1ccc2C(=O)N(C3CCC(=O)NC3=O)C(=O)c2c1

The cyclobutane uses ring label 1, and that label is reused later for the piperazine. By that point ring 1 has already closed (C1CC2(C1)), so the reuse is valid. Inside the spiro fragment, ring 2 is opened at the spiro carbon and closed at the end of the piperidine (CC2), so it is also balanced. The thiophene closure is C2=C1SC(=C2): the label 2 opens at "C2=C1" and closes at "=C2", and ring 1 closes at the S-bearing carbon, which is consistent with the core above.

SMILES: CN(C)Cc1c(OC)cc(cc1OC)C1=CN(C)C(=O)C2=C1SC(=C2)C(=O)NC1CC2(C1)CCN(CC2)C(=O)CCN1CCN(CC1)c1ccc2C(=O)N(C3CCC(=O)NC3=O)C(=O)c2c1

name: rb_0559
text:
I read the structure in four parts: the xanthene dye, the benzoate ring, the diaza-crown macrocycle, and the methoxyphenyl group.

**Xanthene (rhodamine-type) core.** The top ring carries NMe2, the central ring has an O, and the right ring has a C=N+(Me)2 iminium. The C9 carbon links to the benzoate ring.

**Benzoate ring.** Going around from the carbon attached to C9 (call it C1):
- C1 bears the xanthene.
- C2 is a CH, drawn at the top left of this ring.
- C3 bears the macrocycle nitrogen.
- C4 bears OMe.
- C5 is a CH.
- C6 bears the carboxylate (COO⁻) and sits adjacent to C1.

**Macrocycle.** The ring contains two nitrogens and three oxygens. Starting at the N attached to the benzoate ring (N1):
- N1–CH2CH2–O–CH2CH2–O–CH2CH2–N2, which covers the upper and left portion.
- N2 carries the 2-methoxyphenyl group.
- N2–CH2CH2–O–CH2CH2–N1 closes the ring at the bottom.

Reading the drawing, from N1 up and right the path is CH2CH2–O (top right), then CH2CH2–O (top left), then CH2CH2–N2. From N2 the bottom path is CH2CH2–O (bottom), then CH2CH2 back to N1. This gives 15 ring atoms: 2 N, 3 O and 5 × 2 carbons. That is a 15-membered ring, consistent with a triaza/diaza-crown (a 1-aza-15-crown-5 analogue with one O replaced by N-aryl).

**SMILES assembly.**
- Benzoate ring: c1(c(cc(OC)c(c1)N2CCOCCOCCN(CCOCC2)c3ccccc3OC)C(=O)[O-])
- Xanthene attachment: C1 carries the xanthene carbon.
- Xanthene: c1ccc2c(c1)... written with the iminium as C=[N+](C)C.

Full SMILES:
[O-]C(=O)c1cc(OC)c(cc1C1=C2C=CC(=[N+](C)C)C=C2Oc2cc(N(C)C)ccc21)N1CCOCCOCCN(CCOCC1)c1ccccc1OC

Check on the xanthene: C1(=C2C=CC(=[N+](C)C)C=C2Oc2cc(N(C)C)ccc21). The C9 carbon is double-bonded to C2, a ring carbon of the right ring. In that ring C2 is followed by C=C, then C(=N+), then C=C2, which closes back to the ring-fusion carbon bearing O. This ring has six atoms: C2, C, C, C(=N), C, C2-closure. The C=C2 means the last atom is the other fusion carbon, which connects to O. The left ring is c2cc(NMe2)ccc21, with six atoms, ending at the carbon that closes to C9. This is consistent.

The ring-closure label 1 is reused: the first 1 on the benzoate ring is closed at "c1" after the substituent, but I reopened it for the xanthene C1 while the benzoate ring was still open. To avoid a clash I rename the labels.

SMILES: [O-]C(=O)c1cc(OC)c(cc1C3=C4C=CC(=[N+](C)C)C=C4Oc4cc(N(C)C)ccc43)N5CCOCCOCCN(CCOCC5)c6ccccc6OC

text:
I read the molecule as a macrocycle in which two identical benzimidazole units are joined by an (E)-but-2-ene-1,4-diyl chain and by a shared ether linker.

**Each benzimidazole unit**

- C2 carries an NH–C(=O) amide to a 1-ethyl-3-methylpyrazol-5-yl group.
- C5 carries a primary carboxamide (CONH2).
- C7 carries an ether oxygen.

**Butenyl linker**
- N1 of the top unit is joined to N1 of the bottom unit through CH2–CH=CH–CH2.
- The two CH2 groups sit on opposite sides of the double bond in the drawing, so I assigned it as E (trans).

**Ether linker**
- Each C7 oxygen is bonded to a CH2, and both CH2 groups meet at one central CH.
- That CH also carries a CH2CH2 chain ending at C4 of a 1,3-oxazinane ring (C4–C5–C6–O1–C2–N3, with NH at position 3).
- The central CH and the ring C4 are stereocentres by connectivity, but the drawing shows only plain bonds there, so I gave them no stereo marks.

**Ring closures**
- Ring label 3 closes the macrocycle at the top unit's C7 oxygen.
- Ring labels 1 and 2 are reused for the bottom benzimidazole and the oxazinane once earlier closures are complete.

I read this as a cyclic hexapeptide: hexanoyl‑Asp‑His‑D‑1Nal‑Arg‑Trp, with the Asp side‑chain carboxyl closing the ring onto the Trp C‑terminus through a pentane‑1,5‑diamine linker.

- **Asp:** its side‑chain C=O forms an amide with one NH of the –NH(CH2)5NH– linker. I counted five CH2 groups in the linker from the drawing; this count is the least certain part of the reading.
- **His:** an imidazole side chain.
- **Nal:** a 1‑naphthylmethyl side chain.
- **Arg:** a –(CH2)3–NH–C(=NH)NH2 side chain.
- **Trp:** an indol‑3‑ylmethyl side chain. Its C=O forms the amide with the other NH of the linker, which closes the macrocycle.

**Stereochemistry from the wedges and hashes**
- **Asp:** the side‑chain CH2 is on a wedge, which gives the L configuration.
- **His:** the side‑chain CH2 is hashed, which I read as L.
- **Nal:** the CH2 is on a wedge, which gives D.
- **Arg:** the CH2 is hashed, which gives L.
- **Trp:** the CH2 is hashed, which gives L.

name: rb_0561
text:
The structure is a PROTAC-like molecule. I read it in four pieces.

**Right-hand fragment.** A thieno[3,2-c]pyridin-4-one core carries an N-methyl group on the ring nitrogen and a C=O at position 4. Position 7 bears an aryl group, and the carboxamide sits at C2 of the thiophene.
- Thiophene ring: S1, C2 (carboxamide), C3 (CH), C3a, C7a.
- Pyridone ring: C3a is bonded to C4(=O), then N5(Me), C6(H)=C7(Ar), then C7a, which is bonded to S.
- SMILES for the core: c1(C(=O)N...)cc2c(s1)c(Ar)cn(C)c2=O.

**Aryl group.** A phenyl ring with a CH2N(CH3)2 group at the para position and an OMe at each of the two positions flanking it: c1c(OC)c(CN(C)C)c(OC)cc1.

**Spiro linker.** The amide NH is attached to a cyclobutane carbon. The cyclobutane is spiro-fused to a piperidine, which makes a 7-azaspiro[3.5]nonane with the piperidine nitrogen as position 7. The amide-bearing carbon is C2, so the unit is NC1CC2(C1)CCN(CC2)Ar.

**Left-hand fragment.** The piperidine nitrogen is bonded to an isoindolinone ring. The lactam C=O is adjacent to the aromatic carbon next to the one carrying the piperidine N, and the other lactam atom is N, which bears a 2,6-dioxopiperidin-3-yl group.
- Isoindolinone: N1(C2CCC(=O)NC2=O)Cc2ccc(N...)cc2C1=O.

**Assembled SMILES.**
CN(C)Cc1c(OC)cc(cc1OC)-c1cn(C)c(=O)c2cc(sc12)C(=O)NC1CC2(C1)CCN(CC2)c1ccc2CN(C3CCC(=O)NC3=O)C(=O)c2c1

SMILES: CN(C)Cc1c(OC)cc(cc1OC)-c1cn(C)c(=O)c2cc(sc12)C(=O)NC1CC2(C1)CCN(CC2)c1ccc2CN(C3CCC(=O)NC3=O)C(=O)c2c1

name: rb_0558
text:
I read this as an N‑acetylated cyclic heptapeptide, Ac‑Nle‑cyclo[Asp‑His‑(p‑Cl)Phe‑Arg‑Trp] with a diaminoalkane bridge. The Asp side‑chain carbonyl is joined by an amide to the NH of a –(CH2)n–NH linker, and the linker's other NH is the amide on the Trp carbonyl.

Points I was unsure of:

**Tert-leucine.** The alpha carbon bears a tert-butyl group, with the wedge on the N bond. From the 3D arrangement this centre is S.

I checked the three stereocentres against the SMILES chirality tags by working out CIP priorities, and they match the drawing: S for tert-leucine, 4R for the hydroxyl carbon, and 2S for the proline alpha carbon.

- The phenoxazine ring has an N=C bond and an ring O.

- The aromatic ring has OH and CH3 substituents and is fused to a furanone.

**Alkene geometry**

- The CH=CH bond next to the first stereocentre is trans.
- The enol-ether CH=CH is trans.

**Stereocentres**
- Along the chain (amide to ether side) they are @, @, @@, @@, @@, @, @, @@.

I read the molecule as an MDM2-targeting PROTAC. It has a spiro-oxindole/pyrrolidine/cyclohexane core, a PEG-type linker and a thalidomide-type phthalimide end.

**Core**
- The oxindole is 6-chloro, with its C3 spiro-fused to the pyrrolidine.
- The pyrrolidine carries a 3-chloro-2-fluorophenyl group on the carbon next to the oxindole spiro carbon.
- The pyrrolidine carbon next to the NH bears a carboxamide.
- The carbon on the other side of the NH is spiro-fused to a cyclohexane.

**Linker and ligand**
- The carboxamide nitrogen is bonded to a para-substituted benzene.
- The other para position carries C(=O)NH–CH2CH2–O–CH2CH2–O–CH2CH2–O–CH2CH2CH2–.
- The linker ends on the 4-position of an N-(2,6-dioxopiperidin-3-yl)phthalimide. The piperidinedione stereocentre is drawn plainly, so it has no stereo label.

**Stereochemistry**
Three stereocentres are shown with wedges or hashes. I assigned them from the drawn geometry (CIP configurations in parentheses):
- the CH bearing the carboxamide, with a hashed bond (R);
- the CH bearing the aryl group, with a wedge (S);
- the oxindole spiro carbon, with a hash to the aromatic ring and a wedge to the C=O (R).

The cyclohexane spiro carbon is not a stereocentre because the ring is symmetric.

SMILES: O=C(Nc1ccc(cc1)C(=O)NCCOCCOCCOCCCc1cccc2C(=O)N(C3CCC(=O)NC3=O)C(=O)c12)[C@@H]1NC2(CCCCC2)[C@]3(c4ccc(Cl)cc4NC3=O)[C@H]1c1cccc(Cl)c1F

name: rb_0695
text:
I read the molecule left to right as one chain: a pyridine amide, a benzyl linker, a pentanamide spacer, and then a VHL-type ligand.

1. **Left end:** a cyclohexyl group carries an E-vinyl (CH=CH) that attaches at C4 of a pyridine. The pyridine has OMe at C5 and a carboxamide at C2.
2. **Linker:** the carboxamide nitrogen bears a CH2 on a benzene ring. At the meta position of that ring is CH2C(=O)NH.
3. **Spacer:** the NH is followed by four CH2 groups and then C(=O)NH. I counted four CH2 vertices between the NH and the carbonyl.
4. **tert-Leucine:** the next unit is a tert-butyl-bearing stereocentre drawn with a wedge, which I took as the L (S) configuration. Its carbonyl joins the proline nitrogen.
5. **Hydroxyproline:** a 4-hydroxypyrrolidine with the OH on a hash bond and the 2-carboxamide on a wedge. This matches the usual (2S,4R) VHL ligand. I derived the @/@@ labels by converting the known VH032 stereo-SMILES to my atom ordering.
6. **Right end:** the proline amide NH is attached to a CH2 on a para-substituted benzene. The benzene's other end carries a 4-methylthiazol-5-yl group.

The double bond is drawn trans, so it is written `/C=C/`.

SMILES: COc1cnc(C(=O)NCc2cccc(CC(=O)NCCCCC(=O)N[C@@H](C(C)(C)C)C(=O)N3C[C@H](O)C[C@H]3C(=O)NCc3ccc(cc3)-c3scnc3C)c2)cc1/C=C/C1CCCCC1

name: rb_0698
text:
I read the structure in four pieces and joined them into one SMILES.

- **Left end:** a pyridine with a 5-OMe, a 2-carboxamide, and a 4-vinyl group. The vinyl is drawn trans (E). It joins a cyclohexane bearing a CF3 at the 4-position. The hashed bond at the ring carbon bearing the vinyl and the wedge at the CF3 carbon are on opposite faces, so the ring is trans-1,4.
- **Middle:** the amide NH–CH2 is attached to a benzene ring at the 1-position, and the meta (3-) position carries CH2–C(=O)–N(CH3). The N-methyl amide is followed by a chain of the form N–CH2CH2–O–CH2CH2–O–CH2CH2–O–CH2CH2–O. That is three ether oxygens plus the aryl ether oxygen, four in total.
- **Right end:** the chain ends in an aryl ether at the 5-position of a phthalimide (isoindoline-1,3-dione). Its imide nitrogen carries a 2,6-dioxopiperidin-3-yl group, whose stereocentre is drawn plain, so it gets no stereo label.
- **Stereo:** the 1,4-trans cyclohexane is written as `[C@H]1CC[C@@H](...)CC1`, the same pattern as trans-1,4-dimethylcyclohexane. The alkene is `/C=C/`.

SMILES: COc1cnc(C(=O)NCc2cccc(CC(=O)N(C)CCOCCOCCOCCOc3ccc4C(=O)N(C5CCC(=O)NC5=O)C(=O)c4c3)c2)cc1/C=C/[C@H]1CC[C@@H](C(F)(F)F)CC1

name: rb_0697
text:
I read the molecule in four parts and then fixed the stereocentre.

1. **Left end:** a 2,6-dioxopiperidin-3-yl (glutarimide) ring is attached to the nitrogen of a phthalimide. The glutarimide carbon is drawn with plain bonds, so it gets no stereo label.
2. **Linker:** the phthalimide carries an O–CH2–C(=O)–NH group at the 4-position. This continues into a chain of six CH2 groups (counted vertex by vertex), ending at the nitrogen of a piperidine ring.
3. **Piperidine:** the ring carbon at position 3 bears an NH group on a bold wedge. The NH links to C2 of a pyrimidine. That pyrimidine has Cl at C5 and an indol-3-yl group at C4.
4. **Stereochemistry:** I assigned the wedged carbon by CIP priority. The substituents rank NH, then ring C2 (attached to N), then ring C4, then H. With the NH on the wedge, H points away from the viewer. Going NH → C2 → C4 on the page is clockwise, so the centre is R.

In the SMILES, the ring is written as N4CCC[C@@H](N…)C4. In that atom order the neighbours of the stereocentre are C4, H, N, C2, and `@@` encodes the R configuration.

SMILES: O=C1CCC(N2C(=O)c3c(OCC(=O)NCCCCCCN4CCC[C@@H](Nc5ncc(Cl)c(-c6c[nH]c7ccccc67)n5)C4)cccc3C2=O)C(=O)N1

name: rb_0699
text:
I read the structure in four pieces and then joined them.

**Glutarimide and isoindolinone (left).** The glutarimide is O=C1CCC(C(=O)N1)... with its C3 attached to the isoindolinone N. The isoindolinone has a C=O, an N, and a CH2 at C1. The benzo ring carries a piperidin-4-yl group at C7 (next to the CH2) and F at C5. Going around the benzo ring: C3a (attached to C=O), C4 (H), C5 (F), C6 (H), C7 (piperidine), C7a (attached to CH2).

**Isoindolinone SMILES.** O=C1N(C2CCC(=O)NC2=O)Cc2c1cc(F)cc2C3CCN(CC3)...

**Linker.** The piperidine N carries CH2CH2 to a para-disubstituted benzene. The other para position carries CH2CH2O.

**Aryl ether and quinazoline (right).** The O is attached to a phenyl ring. That ring has F at one ortho position and the quinazoline at the other ortho position. The quinazoline is attached at C7 of the quinazoline ring system. Its substituents are:
- C8 has F.
- C6 has Cl.
- C4 has the piperazine.
- N1 and N3 are the ring nitrogens.

The ring atoms run C4a, C5 (H), C6 (Cl), C7 (aryl), C8 (F), C8a, then N1, C2 (H), N3, C4 (piperazine). The piperazine N is acylated with C(=O)C(Cl)=C.

**Quinazoline SMILES.** c1(N2CCN(CC2)C(=O)C(Cl)=C)ncnc3c(F)c(-c4c(F)cccc4OCC...)c(Cl)cc13

**Full SMILES.** O=C1CCC(N2Cc3c(cc(F)cc3C3CCN(CCc4ccc(CCOc5cccc(F)c5-c5c(Cl)cc6c(N7CCN(CC7)C(=O)C(Cl)=C)ncnc6c5F)cc4)CC3)C2=O)C(=O)N1

I checked the isoindolinone part of this string. The ring N2 is followed by CH2 (the C is lowercase c3 as the ring atom). The c3 atom is C7a, bonded to CH2. The next atom, c(cc(F)cc3...), is meant to be C3a, but I wrote it as a branch off the wrong atom. Re-deriving it properly gives: N2Cc3c(C2=O)cc(F)cc3C4CCN(...)CC4.

Here c3 is C7a (attached to CH2). The following c(C2=O) is C3a, which closes the lactam. Then cc(F)c gives C4, C5 (F) and C6. Finally c3 is C7, which closes the ring to C7a and carries the piperidine. This matches the drawing.

SMILES: O=C1CCC(N2Cc3c(C2=O)cc(F)cc3C3CCN(CCc4ccc(CCOc5cccc(F)c5-c5c(Cl)cc6c(N7CCN(CC7)C(=O)C(Cl)=C)ncnc6c5F)cc4)CC3)C(=O)N1

name: rb_0702
text:
The structure breaks into four parts, read left to right.

**Left end:** a pyridine bearing CF3 at the 6-position and a carboxamide at the 2-position. As SMILES: FC(F)(F)c1cccc(n1)C(=O)N–.

**Indazole core:** the amide NH is attached to C5 of a 2H-indazole. C6 carries C(OH)(CF3)CH3. N2 carries the spiro group.
- Ring atoms: c1 (C5, bearing NH), then c (C6, bearing the carbinol), then c (C7, H), c7a, n (N1), n (N2, substituted), c3 (H), c3a, then c4 (H) back to C5.
- SMILES for the core: c1(NC(=O)...)c(C(O)(C)C(F)(F)F)cc2nn(R)cc2c1

**Spiro linker:** 2-azaspiro... specifically a spiro[3.5]nonane. The cyclobutane CH is attached to N2 of the indazole, and the spiro carbon is shared with a piperidine whose nitrogen is acylated.
- SMILES: C1C2(C1)CCN(CC2)C(=O)...
- With the attachment point on the cyclobutane: N2–C1CC2(C1)CCN(CC2)C(=O)

**Right end:** the acyl group is a piperidine-4-carbonyl. The piperidine nitrogen is attached to C5 of an isoindoline-1,3-dione. The isoindoline N carries a 2,6-dioxopiperidin-3-yl group.
- Piperidine part: C4CCN(CC4)c5ccc6c(c5)C(=O)N(C7CCC(=O)NC7=O)C6=O

**Full SMILES:**
FC(F)(F)c1cccc(n1)C(=O)Nc1cc2cn(nc2cc1C(O)(C)C(F)(F)F)C1CC2(C1)CCN(CC2)C(=O)C1CCN(CC1)c1ccc2C(=O)N(C3CCC(=O)NC3=O)C(=O)c2c1

The ring-closure digits are reused after their rings close, which is valid. I checked the isoindoline: c1ccc2C(=O)N(...)C(=O)c2c1 puts the piperidine N-bearing carbon in the right position (C5, para to one carbonyl-bearing carbon). The drawing shows plain bonds at the glutarimide stereocentre, so no stereochemistry is included.

SMILES: FC(F)(F)c1cccc(n1)C(=O)Nc1cc2cn(nc2cc1C(O)(C)C(F)(F)F)C1CC2(C1)CCN(CC2)C(=O)C1CCN(CC1)c1ccc2C(=O)N(C3CCC(=O)NC3=O)C(=O)c2c1

name: rb_0703
text:
I read the structure in four pieces and then joined them.

**Left fragment.** A pyridine ring carries CF3 at C6 and a carboxamide at C2: FC(F)(F)c1cccc(n1)C(=O)N-.

**Indazole.** The amide NH is attached at C5 of a 2H-indazole. The ring is drawn as an aromatic benzene fused to a pyrazole, with OMe at C6 and the N2 substituent at the spiro unit. The SMILES is c1(NC(=O)...)c(OC)cc2nn(R)cc2c1.

**Spiro unit.** The indazole N2 is bonded to a cyclobutane carbon. The cyclobutane is spiro-fused to a piperidine, giving 2,7-diazaspiro[3.5]nonane-like geometry, except that here the 2-position is a carbon. The ring is C1CC2(C1)CCN(CC2)C(=O)..., which is 7-azaspiro[3.5]nonane. The piperidine N is acylated by the carbonyl.

**Right fragment.** The carbonyl attaches at C4 of a piperidine. That piperidine's N is bonded to C5 of an isoindoline-1,3-dione. The imide N carries a 2,6-dioxopiperidin-3-yl group: C(=O)C1CCN(CC1)c1ccc2c(c1)C(=O)N(C2=O)C1CCC(=O)NC1=O.

**Assembled SMILES.** The one stereocentre (the glutarimide C3) is drawn with plain bonds, so no stereo is specified.

SMILES: FC(F)(F)c1cccc(n1)C(=O)Nc1cc2cn(nc2cc1OC)C1CC2(C1)CCN(CC2)C(=O)C1CCN(CC1)c1ccc2C(=O)N(C3CCC(=O)NC3=O)C(=O)c2c1

name: rb_0704
text:
I read the structure in four pieces and then joined them.

**Left fragment.** A 6-methylpyridine-2-carboxamide: Cc1cccc(n1)C(=O)N–. The amide NH is attached to C5 of a 2H-indazole. The indazole carries a methoxy group on C6, and N2 is attached to the spiro system.

**Indazole.** The benzene ring carbons are C5 (bearing NH), C6 (bearing OMe), C7 (CH), C7a (bonded to N1), C3a and C4 (CH). The pyrazole ring is N2(R)–C3H=C3a, with N1 bonded to C7a. As SMILES: c1(NC(=O)...)c(OC)cc2nn(R)cc2c1.

**Spiro linker.** The N2 substituent is a cyclobutane CH. It is spiro-fused through the opposite cyclobutane carbon to a piperidine, giving 7-azaspiro[3.5]nonane. The piperidine nitrogen is acylated. As SMILES: C1(C2)CC2(CC1)... Written out: N2–C1CC2(C1)CCN(CC2)C(=O)...

**Right fragment.** The acyl group is a piperidine-4-carbonyl. The piperidine nitrogen is attached to C5 of a phthalimide, and the phthalimide N bears a 2,6-dioxopiperidin-3-yl group. As SMILES: C(=O)C1CCN(CC1)c1ccc2C(=O)N(C3CCC(=O)NC3=O)C(=O)c2c1.

**Assembled SMILES:**
Cc1cccc(n1)C(=O)Nc1cc2cn(nc2cc1OC)C1CC2(C1)CCN(CC2)C(=O)C1CCN(CC1)c1ccc2C(=O)N(C3CCC(=O)NC3=O)C(=O)c2c1

Check on the indazole: c1cc2cn(nc2cc1OC) begins at C5 (bearing NH), then c is C4, c2 is C3a, c is C3, n(...) is N2, n is N1, c2 is C7a, c is C7, and c1OC is C6, which closes the ring to C5. This is correct.

No stereochemistry is drawn, so none is included.

SMILES: Cc1cccc(n1)C(=O)Nc1cc2cn(nc2cc1OC)C1CC2(C1)CCN(CC2)C(=O)C1CCN(CC1)c1ccc2C(=O)N(C3CCC(=O)NC3=O)C(=O)c2c1

name: rb_0705
text:
Reading the structure from left to right:

1. **Morpholine–pyridine amide.** Morpholine N is attached to C6 of a pyridine. The pyridine C2 carries the C(=O)NH amide. SMILES fragment: O=C(Nc...)c1cccc(N2CCOCC2)n1.

2. **2H-indazole.** The amide NH is on C5. C6 carries OMe. The ring N2 is attached to the cyclobutane. The 2H-indazole is written c1cc2cn(...)nc2cc1OC, with the NH at C5.
   - Atoms: C5 (NH) – C4 (H) – C3a – C3 (H) = N2(R) – N1 = C7a – C7 (H) – C6 (OMe) – C5.
   - SMILES: Nc1cc2cn(R)nc2cc1OC.

3. **Spiro linker.** The cyclobutane CH is bonded to N2. The cyclobutane's opposite carbon is the spiro carbon, which belongs to a piperidine. This is a 7-azaspiro[3.5]nonane: C1CC(C1)... with the spiro carbon in a piperidine ring whose N is acylated. SMILES: C1(CC2(C1)CCN(CC2)C(=O)...).

4. **Acyl piperidine.** The C(=O) is attached to C4 of a piperidine that also carries F. The piperidine N is attached to C5 of the phthalimide (isoindoline-1,3-dione). The phthalimide N bears the 2,6-dioxopiperidin-3-yl group. The glutarimide stereocentre has no wedge, so no stereo is given.
   - SMILES: C(=O)C1(F)CCN(CC1)c1ccc2c(c1)C(=O)N(C3CCC(=O)NC3=O)C2=O.

Assembled:

O=C(Nc1cc2cn(nc2cc1OC)C1CC2(C1)CCN(CC2)C(=O)C1(F)CCN(CC1)c1ccc2c(c1)C(=O)N(C1CCC(=O)NC1=O)C2=O)c1cccc(N2CCOCC2)n1

name: rb_0700
text:
I read this as a bifunctional degrader. A spiro-oxindole pyrrolidine (an MDM2-type ligand) is joined through a nicotinamide and a PEG-type linker to a pomalidomide unit. I wrote the SMILES in four parts.

1. **Pomalidomide end:** the 4-amino-isoindoline-1,3-dione carries the 2,6-dioxopiperidin-3-yl group on its imide nitrogen. The aryl NH leaves the ring and starts the linker. The piperidine stereocentre is drawn with plain bonds, so it has no stereo label.
2. **Linker:** from the aryl NH the chain is CH2CH2CH2–O–CH2CH2–O–CH2CH2–O–CH2CH2CH2–NH–C(=O). That is 3 + 2 + 2 + 3 chain carbons with three ether oxygens. The chain ends in an amide to the pyridine.
3. **Pyridine:** the amide carbon sits at position 5. An NH–C(=O) at position 2 connects to the pyrrolidine core.
4. **Core:** the central pyrrolidine has these positions:
   - C2 carries the C(=O)NH amide on a hashed bond.
   - C3 carries the 3-chloro-2-fluorophenyl on a wedge.
   - C4 is the spiro carbon of the 6-chlorooxindole. Its hashed bond goes to the aromatic ring and its wedge bond to the lactam C=O.
   - C5 is the spiro cyclohexane carbon. Its two ring arms are identical, so it gets no stereo label.

I assigned @/@@ from the wedge and hash geometry at the three stereocentres. The SMILES was checked by hand only, not run through a validator.

SMILES: O=C1NC(=O)CCC1N1C(=O)c2cccc(NCCCOCCOCCOCCCNC(=O)c3ccc(NC(=O)[C@@H]4NC5(CCCCC5)[C@]6(c7ccc(Cl)cc7NC6=O)[C@H]4c4cccc(Cl)c4F)nc3)c2C1=O

text:

name: rb_0701
text:
I read the molecule as a PROTAC-style conjugate. A spiro-oxindole MDM2-type ligand is joined through a trans-cyclohexane diamide and a triethylene-glycol diamine linker to a lenalidomide-type glutarimide ligand. I worked through it region by region.

- **Right-hand end:** a 4-amino isoindolin-1-one carries N-linked 2,6-dioxopiperidin-3-yl, written `Nc1cccc2c1CN(C2=O)C1CCC(=O)NC1=O`. The glutarimide carbon is drawn with plain bonds, so it gets no stereo label.
- **Linker:** from the isoindolinone NH the chain is CH2CH2–O–CH2CH2–O–CH2CH2–O–CH2CH2–NH. The chain ends at the carbonyl of a cyclohexane carboxamide.
- **Cyclohexane:** it is 1,4-disubstituted, with a wedge on the carboxamide carbon and a hash on the carbon bearing the NH. That is trans, written `[C@H]1CC[C@@H](...)CC1`.
- **Spiro core:** the NH–C(=O) on the cyclohexane is a carboxamide on the pyrrolidine ring. The pyrrolidine ring runs NH, CH(C=O), CH(3-chlorophenyl), then the spiro carbon of a 6-chloro-oxindole, then the spiro carbon of a cyclohexane. The second spiro carbon is not a stereocentre because the cyclohexane is symmetric.
- **Stereocentres:** I assigned the three pyrrolidine centres from the wedges and hashes. The carboxamide carbon has a hash on its C=O. The aryl-bearing carbon has a wedge to the aryl group. The oxindole spiro carbon has a hash to the aromatic carbon and a wedge to the lactam C=O.

I checked the ring closures and valences by hand and the SMILES is valid.

name: rb_0709
text:
I read the structure region by region, from the left-hand kinase-binding end to the thalidomide-type end on the right.

**Left end.** An indoline is attached through its C7 to an NH. Its N1 carries a methylsulfonyl group, and the ring has CH2CH2 at positions 2 and 3. The NH links to C4 of a pyrimidine. The pyrimidine has Br at C5 and an NH at C2, and C6 is a CH.

**Central aryl ring.** The C2 NH connects to a benzene ring. Going around that ring, the substituents are:
- NH at position 1
- OMe at position 2
- H at position 3
- piperidin-1-yl at position 4
- methyl at position 5
- H at position 6

This follows the image: the NH-bearing carbon sits at the left, the OMe carbon is above it, the next carbon is CH, then the carbon bearing the piperidine N, then the carbon bearing the methyl, then a CH back to the start.

**Linker.** The aryl-bound piperidine is attached at its C4 to a piperazine N. The other piperazine N is attached to C4 of a second piperidine, whose N is bonded to the isoindoline-dione ring.

**Right end.** The isoindoline-1,3-dione carries the piperidine N at position 5. Its imide N is bonded to C3 of a 2,6-dioxopiperidine. The drawing shows no stereo wedges, so no stereochemistry is given.

**SMILES assembly.**
- Indoline: CS(=O)(=O)N1CCc2cccc(N...)c21

I read the molecule as a PROTAC-type conjugate and assembled the SMILES in pieces, working left to right across the drawing.

**Fragments**

- **Aryl group:** a 3-chloro-2-fluorophenyl sits on the pyrrolidine carbon next to the spiro-oxindole carbon.
- **Amide to the cage:** the pyrrolidine carbon bearing the carbonyl is joined through C(=O)NH to a bicyclo[2.2.2]octane bridgehead. The opposite bridgehead carries a second C(=O)NH.
- **Linker:** NH–CH2CH2CH2–O–CH2CH2–O–CH2CH2–O–CH2CH2CH2–NH–C(=O)CH2–O.
- **Thalidomide end:** the oxygen is attached to the 4-position of the phthalimide ring, which is N-linked to a 2,6-dioxopiperidin-3-yl group.

**Stereochemistry**
- The drawing shows wedges or hashes at three stereocentres: the CH bearing the carbonyl (hashed), the CH bearing the aryl group (wedged), and the spiro oxindole carbon (hashed to the aromatic ring, wedged to the lactam C=O).
- I worked out the @/@@ labels from the 2D geometry by hand and did not check them with software.
- The glutarimide CH and the spiro-cyclohexane carbon are drawn without wedges, so they carry no stereo label.
