name: rb_0840
text:
The SMILES below was read from the drawing region by region.

- **Left fragment:** a 6,7-dihydro-5H-benzo[7]annulene with a phenolic OH on the benzo ring. The seven-membered ring carries a tetrasubstituted C=C. One alkene carbon bears a 4-(piperidin-1-yl)phenyl group, and the other bears a 4-(trifluoromethoxy)phenyl group. Three CH2 groups complete the ring.
- **Linker:** the piperidine is substituted at C4 by a CH2 that connects to a piperazine nitrogen.
- **Right fragment:** the other piperazine nitrogen is attached to C5 of an isoindolin-1-one. That aryl carbon is para to the ring carbon bearing the CH2, and meta to the carbon bearing the C=O. The lactam nitrogen is attached to C3 of a piperidine-2,6-dione (glutarimide).
- **Stereochemistry:** the glutarimide C3 is drawn with a hashed bond to the lactam nitrogen, which puts that nitrogen behind the plane. Working through the CIP priorities (N > C(=O) > CH2 > H) gives the S configuration, which is written as `[C@H]` in this SMILES. The alkene is in a ring and has no cis/trans marking in the drawing, so I added no geometry to it.

name: rb_0842
text:
I read the structure in five parts and joined them into one SMILES.

- **Glutarimide:** a piperidine-2,6-dione ring attached at its 3-position to the isoindolinone nitrogen.
- **Isoindolinone:** a lactam with the C=O next to the aromatic ring and a CH2 on the other side. The benzo ring carries a fluorine and a 4-piperidinyl group. The fluorine sits meta to the piperidinyl group, and the piperidinyl group is on the carbon next to the one bearing the CH2.
- **Linker:** the piperidine nitrogen carries a straight chain of 7 CH2 groups ending in an ether oxygen. I counted seven zigzag vertices between the nitrogen and the oxygen, but this count is the least certain part of the reading.
- **Aryl ether:** a phenyl ring bearing the O, a fluorine on one ortho carbon, and the quinazoline on the other ortho carbon.
- **Quinazoline:** C4 bears a piperazine whose far nitrogen is acryloylated (N-C(=O)CH=CH2). C5 is CH, C6 has Cl, C7 has the aryl group, and C8 has F.

The drawing shows no wedges, hashes or cis/trans bonds, so I added no stereochemistry. The ring-closure numbers are reused only after each ring is closed, so the SMILES is valid.

name: rb_0844
text:
The structure is a PROTAC-like molecule: an estrogen-receptor-binding benzocycloheptene fragment, a phenyl-piperidine linked through CH2 to a piperazine, and a lenalidomide-type isoindolinone-glutarimide.

**Benzocycloheptene fragment.**
- The aromatic ring carries an OH.
- It is fused to a seven-membered ring: the aromatic carbons C4a and C9a, then C5(aryl)=C6(Ph), then CH2CH2CH2 back to the aromatic ring.
- The ring atoms are Ar-C(=C(Ph)CCC-Ar), so the seven members are two aromatic carbons, two alkene carbons and three CH2 groups.
- The alkene carbon next to the aromatic ring bears the 4-substituted phenyl. The other alkene carbon bears a phenyl.

SMILES for this part: Oc1ccc2c(c1)CCCC(c1ccccc1)=C2c1ccc(cc1)N1CCC(CC1)CN1CCN(CC1)...

Reading the ring: the OH-bearing carbon is c1, then cc, then c2, which is the aromatic carbon attached to the alkene carbon C(Ar). The other fusion carbon is attached to CH2.

**Piperidine and piperazine.** The phenyl nitrogen is a piperidine N. Position 4 of the piperidine carries CH2, which connects to a piperazine N. The other piperazine N is attached to the isoindolinone at position 5.

**Isoindolinone.**
- The aromatic ring has the piperazine at one carbon. The C=O carbon is attached to the ring carbon para to the piperazine-bearing carbon, and CH2 is attached to the ring carbon meta to it.
- In the drawing, the piperazine-bearing carbon is at the top, adjacent to the ring-fusion carbon that carries the C=O side.
- Writing the ring as c1ccc2c(c1)CN(C2=O)C3CCC(=O)NC3=O, the piperazine-bearing carbon is the first atom c1. Its neighbours are c (CH) and the c(c1) atom, which carries the CH2.
- Here the piperazine carbon is attached to a CH that is attached to the CH2-bearing carbon, and also to a CH that leads to the C=O-bearing carbon. This matches the drawing.

**Glutarimide.** The stereocentre is drawn with plain bonds, so no stereo is given.

SMILES: Oc1ccc2c(c1)CCCC(c1ccccc1)=C2c1ccc(cc1)N1CCC(CC1)CN1CCN(CC1)c1ccc2C(=O)N(Cc2c1)C1CCC(=O)NC1=O

name: rb_0845
text:
Reading the structure from left to right:

1. Left end: a methylsulfonyl group (CH3-S(=O)(=O)) on the nitrogen of a pyrrole. The ring is N1, C2, C3 (bearing the carboxamide), C4, C5. The ring is drawn with N at the bottom left, an upper carbon, then C3 bearing the C(=O), so it is a pyrrole-3-carboxamide: CS(=O)(=O)n1ccc(c1)C(=O)N...
2. The amide NH connects to CH2, then C(=O)NH on thiazole C2: C(=O)NCC(=O)Nc1nc(cs1)...
3. Thiazole: S, C2 (bearing NH), N3, C4 (bearing the aryl group), C5 (H). The C4 aryl is a biphenyl; both rings are meta-linked. The second ring carries CH2NH.
4. Chain: CH2-NH-C(=O)-CH2CH2-O-CH2CH2-O-CH2CH2-NH-Ar.
5. Right end: the aryl ring is the isoindoline-1,3-dione (phthalimide) with NH at position 4, and the imide N bears a 2,6-dioxopiperidin-3-yl group. This is the pomalidomide unit.

SMILES assembly:
CS(=O)(=O)n1ccc(c1)C(=O)NCC(=O)Nc1nc(cs1)-c1cccc(c1)-c1cccc(c1)CNC(=O)CCOCCOCCNc1cccc2c1C(=O)N(C2=O)C1CCC(=O)NC1=O

The pyrrole SMILES n1ccc(c1)C(=O) gives N1, C2, C3, C4(substituted), C5, so the substituent sits on the carbon adjacent to C5 and is a 3-substituent. Written as n1ccc(c1)..., the atoms are n1, c, c, c(substituted), c1 closing to n. That makes the substituted carbon adjacent to the closing carbon, which is adjacent to N, so it is position 3. This matches the drawing.

SMILES: CS(=O)(=O)n1ccc(c1)C(=O)NCC(=O)Nc1nc(cs1)-c1cccc(c1)-c1cccc(c1)CNC(=O)CCOCCOCCNc1cccc2c1C(=O)N(C2=O)C1CCC(=O)NC1=O

text:
I read the structure in four pieces and then joined them.

**Left end.** A pyridine carries CF3 at the 6-position and a carboxamide at C2. The amide NH is bonded to C5 of the indazole.

**Indazole.** It is a 2H-indazole, with N2 substituted.
- C5 carries the NHC(=O) group.
- C6 carries C(C)(C)O, a 2-hydroxypropan-2-yl group.
- N2 is bonded to the spiro ring.

**Spiro system.** A cyclobutane carries the indazole N2 at its 2-position. Its spiro carbon is shared with a piperidine, which gives a 7-azaspiro[3.5]nonane. The piperidine N is acylated.

**Right side.** The acyl group is a piperidine-4-carbonyl. That piperidine's N is attached to C5 of an isoindoline-1,3-dione, and the isoindoline N carries a 2,6-dioxopiperidin-3-yl group. The glutarimide carbon is a stereocentre but is drawn with plain bonds, so I give it no stereo.

- Pyridine amide: FC(F)(F)c1cccc(n1)C(=O)N
- Indazole: c2cc3cn(nc3cc2C(C)(C)O)
- Spiro piece: C4CC5(C4)CCN(CC5)C(=O)
- Piperidine and phthalimide: C6CCN(CC6)c7ccc8c(c7)C(=O)N(C8=O)C9CCC(=O)NC9=O

I checked the ring closures. In the indazole, c1cc2cn(nc2cc1C...) closes the benzene ring correctly: c1 (C5), c (C4), c2 (C3a), c (C3), n (N2) with its substituent, n (N1), c2 (C7a), c (C7), c1 (C6). Closing label 1 reuses the number after it has closed, which is fine.

**Glycine linker.** The amide NH connects to CH2, then C(=O), then NH on the thiazole C2: ...C(=O)NCC(=O)Nc1nc(cs1)...

**Middle chain.** N(C)CC(=O)NC1CCN(CC1)CCOc... The piperidine C4 carries the NH, and the piperidine N carries CH2CH2-O-aryl.

**Right end.** The aryl group is the isoindoline-1,3-dione benzene ring with the O at position 5. The imide N is attached to a 2,6-dioxopiperidin-3-yl group. The stereocentre there is drawn with plain bonds, so I give it no stereo.

The carbonyl-bearing atom is the third one after N going the long way round and the second one going the short way round (via c1), so it is position 3. This is correct.

**Pyridine.** c1ccnc(c1)N(C)...: the first atom c1 is the aryl-attached C4, then c (C5), c (C6), n (N1), c (C2, bearing N(C)), and c1 (C3) closes the ring. This is correct.
